findings.title: Track-card header shows dual script in transliteration mode — Hebrew 'תלמוד בבלי' rendered under Latin 'Talmud Bavli' (violates EN-mode no-Hebrew oracle rule, and is asymmetric vs Hebrew mode)
findings.permutation: en / adult / populated / Hebrew-terms OFF (Ashkenazi)
findings.evidence: /tmp/audit/zoom_track_header2.png shows 'Talmud Bavli' (small, top) stacked above 'תלמוד בבלי' (large/bold, bottom). Compare /tmp/audit/dash_pop_scroll2.png (Hebrew-terms ON) where the same card shows ONLY 'תלמוד בבלי' with no Latin companion.
findings.detail: Oracle: 'EN / transliteration mode MUST NOT contain Hebrew-script characters (U+0590–U+05FF). A stray Hebrew letter in an English-mode label indicates a missed transliteration.' In transliteration mode the active-track card surfaces the native Hebrew curriculum name as the prominent (larger) title with the Latin transliteration as a small superscript. This both contains Hebrew script in EN-mode AND is asymmetric: Hebrew-terms-ON mode does NOT show a Latin transliteration companion. The position bar ('Chullin 41') and stat tiles correctly stay Latin, so only the curriculum title is dual-script. Needs human confirmation whether the bilingual title is intended; if so the rule/oracle expectation should be documented, otherwise the Hebrew line should be suppressed in transliteration mode.

findings.title: Mixed-script stat chips row: 'Streak' (Latin) | 'סיומים' (Hebrew) | 'Lifetime' (Latin) on one row in EN UI when Hebrew-terms toggle is ON
findings.permutation: en / adult / populated / Hebrew-terms ON
findings.evidence: /tmp/audit/zoom_chiplabels.png ('Streak' / 'סיומים' / 'Lifetime'); resolves to all-Latin 'Streak'/'Siyumim'/'Lifetime' when toggle OFF — see /tmp/audit/dash_translit.png
findings.detail: On the populated dashboard the three summary chips mix scripts: the domain term 'Siyumim' follows the Hebrew-terms toggle and renders as Hebrew script (סיומים), while its row-mates 'Streak' and 'Lifetime' are generic UI labels that stay English. The same pattern appears in the STATS card ('OVERDUE'/'TODAY DUE' English next to 'חזרה' Hebrew — /tmp/audit/zoom_stats3e.png) and the track-card stat tiles ('חזרה'/'DUE TODAY'/'OVERDUE' — /tmp/audit/zoom_tiles.png). This is consistent with the documented independent-axes design (domain terms follow the toggle, generic UI follows locale), so it is arguably by-design, but to a human reviewer a single Hebrew word wedged between two English words on the same chip row reads as a half-translated / inconsistent UI. Flagging for product decision on whether sibling labels should be harmonized (either translate Streak/Lifetime too, or keep Siyumim/Chazara in Latin while toggle drives only curriculum content).

findings.title: App UI locale cannot be switched to Hebrew from within the app or via per-profile pref — UI follows device locale only
findings.permutation: locale lever (he) for all dashboard permutations
findings.evidence: learning_tracker/lib/app/learning_tracker_app.dart:59-61 ('locale: null — Flutter resolves the active locale automatically from WidgetsBinding.window.locale … DNI-341'); settings_screen.dart:197 gates the Hebrew-terms tile on Localizations.localeOf(context).languageCode != 'he'; editing shared_prefs flutter.app_locale_p1=he had ZERO effect on the rendered UI (/tmp/audit/dash_he_adult.png stayed fully English).
findings.detail: The per-profile AppLocalePreference (app_locale_p1) exists and is written by the app, but the MaterialApp uses locale:null so the visible UI locale is driven entirely by the OS device locale; the pref is only consumed for out-of-band rendering (notifications, currentAppLocaleProvider). There is NO in-app UI-language control on the dashboard/settings path (the visible 'Calendar Preference English/Hebrew' is the calendar, not the UI locale). Consequence: (1) the he<->en UI-locale audit lever is not exercisable in this environment — device locale change requires root and adbd cannot run as root on this production build (API 31, no cmd locale service), so all he-locale dashboard chrome (RTL layout, Hebrew nav labels, Hebrew empty-state copy) is UNVERIFIED; (2) more importantly this is a product gap: a user who sets a profile to Hebrew via the app gets no Hebrew UI. Recommend wiring currentAppLocaleProvider into MaterialApp.locale (or a Localizations override) so the per-profile pref actually drives the UI, and to make the he-locale state testable.

findings.title: Reward title breaks mid-word under large text (font_scale 1.3): 'IceCre/am', 'Bicycl/e'

findings.permutation: en / ADULT MODE / Notification Settings sub-screen

findings.title: Hebrew UI leaves 'SHABBOS' untranslated and produces mixed-script 'בShabbos'

findings.title: Sync outbox backlog grows on every settings change and 'Tap to retry' is a no-op

findings.title: Scope item count ignores the user's section selection — uses full-curriculum total (≈5846) instead of the selected sefer
findings.permutation: Chumash flow, Step 5 pace/deadline; reproduced in both he-script mode and transliteration mode
findings.evidence: /tmp/at_en_deadline.png + /tmp/at_helper_s.png — helper text reads 'About 5846 Pesukim per study day, across 1 study days to finish the scope by the deadline (≈5846 items)'. Same '≈5846 items' in he mode at /tmp/at_deadline.png.
findings.detail: Only Bereishis was selected as the scope on Step 2, yet the pace/deadline math uses 5846 items. 5846 ≈ the pesukim total of the ENTIRE 5-book Chumash (Genesis 1533 + Exodus 1213 + Leviticus 859 + Numbers 1288 + Deuteronomy 955 ≈ 5848). Bereishis alone has ~1533 pesukim / 50 perakim. The wizard computes pace feasibility and the 'per study day' figure against the whole curriculum rather than the selected scope, producing wildly wrong estimates and an unachievable deadline. This is a goal-math correctness bug, not a localization issue (wrong in en too).

findings.detail: track_info_card.dart line 116 passes label `l10n.trackInfoElapsed` (="Elapsed"), and the value builder `_elapsedRemainingLabel` (line 165) constructs the value as `'${l10n.trackInfoElapsed} $elapsedDays ${l10n.trackInfoDays}'` = "Elapsed 0 days". findings.title: Same activation date shown in two different calendar systems on one screen (Hebrew "Started" vs Gregorian "Since")
findings.permutation: en-locale + Hebrew calendar ON (all term/nusach states)
findings.evidence: /tmp/td_en_hterms.png — TrackInfoCard "Started" row = "כ\"ה סיוון תשפ\"ו" (Hebrew calendar), while the header card directly below shows "Since Jun 10, 2026" (Gregorian) for the same track.activatedAt.
findings.detail: TrackInfoCard._formatDate honors useHebrewCalendar and renders the Hebrew date for "Started". But track_detail_screen.dart line 173 computes `activatedDate = DateFormat.yMMMd(locale).format(track.activatedAt)` unconditionally in Gregorian, and feeds it to the "Since {date}" line in _buildHeaderCard. So the identical activation date is shown twice in two incompatible calendar formats inches apart, which is confusing. The "Since" line should respect the useHebrewCalendar preference like the InfoCard does.

findings.title: Goal pace field label and helper clipped/ellipsized ("Perakim p…" / "How many …")
findings.permutation: en-locale, reached from the goal tile (Edit Goal → GoalSetupScreen); observed in both HebrewTerms ON ("פרקים per …") and OFF ("Perakim p…")
findings.evidence: /tmp/td_goal_translit.png and /tmp/td_goal_en.png — the pace TextField's floating label reads "Perakim p…" (truncated from "Perakim per week") and the helper text below reads "How many …" (truncated from "How many perakim per week?").
findings.detail: goal_setup_screen.dart line 385 sets `labelText: '$unitLabel $perLabel'` (="Perakim per week") and line 387 `helperText: 'How many perakim per week?'`. The field sits in a narrow box beside the Per day/Per week selector, so both the label and helper are ellipsized and unreadable. The full text never fits. Reachable directly via the TrackDetail goal tile, which this pass was required to exercise.

findings.title: Per-profile UI locale (he) cannot be activated; no in-app UI-language switcher exists
findings.permutation: Attempted en→he for LoopA (profile p1)
findings.evidence: /tmp/td_he_dash3.png and uiautomator dump /tmp/ui_he.xml — after setting flutter.app_locale_p1=he (LoopA's confirmed key, verified via matching hebrew_terms_script_p1/use_hebrew_calendar_p1/transliteration_variant_p1 prefs) and force-stop+relaunch+re-selecting LoopA, the entire UI remained English ("Good evening", "Streak", "Lifetime", "DASHBOARD/LEARN/PROGRESS/SETTINGS"). The Settings screen exposes only a Calendar-Preference English/Hebrew toggle (dates only) and the Hebrew-Terms toggle (term script) — there is NO control to switch the app UI language.
findings.detail: Two concerns: (1) the per-profile app_locale pref written to shared_prefs did not take effect after a clean relaunch, suggesting the locale is restored/overridden from another source (DB/cloud) on profile selection, or the provider is not re-reading it; (2) there is no user-facing way to change the UI language for an existing profile, so a profile stuck in the wrong locale has no in-app remedy. Consequence for this audit: the he-locale RTL rendering of TrackDetail (RTL mirroring of rows, back-arrow placement, Hebrew chrome) could not be visually verified.

findings.title: Chazara/review section could not be visually verified (no multi-stage track available)
findings.permutation: All states — only a single-stage Chumash track exists for LoopA
findings.evidence: /tmp/td_en_hterms.png — header shows plain "Track progress" label, never the "Completion (with חזרה/Chazara)" variant. dashboard_providers.dart trackHasChazaraProvider returns count>1 stages; the Chumash track has 1 stage so chazara UI is (correctly) hidden.
findings.detail: The gating rule (chazara label only for stageOrder>1) is correctly implemented and the negative case is confirmed (single-stage track shows no chazara label, matching `l10n.carouselCompletion(chazaraTerm)` being skipped). However the POSITIVE case — a track with a review stage rendering "Completion (with Chazara)" in English and "השלמה (עם חזרה)" in Hebrew with geresh-marked stage numerals (חזרה א׳) — could not be exercised because no multi-stage track is present in this account. Recommend seeding a multi-stage track to fully verify the chazara term rendering across nusach/script.

findings.title: Track-created toast leaks English translation 'Genesis' instead of transliteration/Hebrew sefer name
findings.permutation: child mode, Hebrew-Terms ON, creating a Chumash > Bereishis track
findings.evidence: /tmp/child_trackdone.png — snackbar reads: Track "Genesis" created. The track card correctly shows חומש, but the confirmation toast used the raw English Bible translation 'Genesis'.
findings.detail: Oracle: a rendered literal 'Genesis'/'Exodus'/'Psalms' in any mode is WRONG for a Chumash sefer — it must be the transliterated Hebrew name (ashkenazi 'Bereishis' / sephardi 'Bereshit') or, in Hebrew-script mode, 'בראשית'. Here the active profile is Hebrew-Terms-ON so the expected name is בראשית; instead the snackbar surfaced the un-transliterated English translation. The sefer-name transliteration/Hebrew override was missed on the toast code path (the curriculum picker and tree render it correctly, so this is a path-specific leak).

findings.title: Same masechta rendered with two different nuschaos in the app (Berakhot vs Berakhos)
findings.permutation: en / ashkenazi (Hebrew-Terms OFF) — Dashboard/Learn daily-task tile vs expanded breadcrumb
findings.evidence: /tmp/back1.png shows the compact daily-task tile as 'Berakhot 2a' (sephardi/raw spelling); /tmp/learn2.png shows the SAME task expanded as 'Berakhos › Daf 2 › Amud a' (ashkenazi). Settings confirm Pronunciation=Ashkenazi (/tmp/settings_lang.png).
findings.detail: With nusach=ashkenazi and Hebrew-Terms OFF the masechta must transliterate to 'Berakhos' (per LevelLabels / name-transliteration map: Berakhos/Berakhot differ by nusach). The compact daily-task label path leaked the raw/sephardi 'Berakhot' while the breadcrumb path and the Progress > Lifetime Knowledge tree (/tmp/life_tree2.png) correctly render 'Berakhos'. Same data, two different transliterations depending on render path = an oracle correctness bug. (Surfaces on Dashboard/Learn; the masechta feeds the Progress breakdown so it is in-scope context — Progress itself renders it correctly.)

findings.title: Plural not handled for count = 1: '1 Items learned' (should be '1 Item learned')
findings.permutation: en / adult / after a single completion — Lifetime Knowledge header (also under large text)
findings.evidence: /tmp/life_after.png and /tmp/life_largetext.png — header reads '1 Items learned' with the plural noun while the count is 1.
findings.detail: English plural/singular agreement is not applied to the items-learned summary count. With exactly one item it reads '1 Items learned'. Minor but visible polish bug on a primary Progress sub-screen header. (In Hebrew-terms mode the phrasing is 'פריטים נלמדו 1' which has no English plural issue, so this is en-chrome specific.)

findings.title: Mixed Latin/Hebrew on Progress hub & Lifetime cards when Hebrew-Terms ON under an English UI locale
findings.permutation: Hebrew-Terms ON, device locale en — Progress hub + Lifetime Knowledge
findings.evidence: /tmp/prog_he_hub.png (🏆 counter label 'סיומים' Hebrew but lens tile 'Siyumim & Milestones' + 'Streak'/'Lifetime' English on the same screen); /tmp/life_he.png ('תלמוד בבלי' Hebrew name directly above '1 of 5349' English chrome); /tmp/life_he_tree4.png ('Live' Latin provenance label inline with 'עמוד א').
findings.detail: The Hebrew-Terms toggle swaps only domain terms (siyumim, curriculum names, chazara) to Hebrew script, while UI chrome ('Streak','Lifetime','Recent Activity','X of Y','Live') follows the device locale (en). This is the documented chrome-vs-term split so it is not strictly an oracle violation, but it produces jarring within-screen mixed-script strings on the lifetime cards and the same concept shown twice in two scripts ('סיומים' counter vs 'Siyumim & Milestones' tile). Worth a product decision; flagged because the oracle warns HE-script content should not carry Latin literals and a reviewer cannot tell intentional-chrome from a leak by eye.

findings.title: No in-app UI-language (he/en) switcher is wired; locale override via shared_prefs has no effect
findings.permutation: attempting the en<->he UI-LOCALE permutation lever
findings.evidence: grep shows LanguageNotifier/setLanguage/supportedLanguages defined only in learning_tracker/lib/core/preferences/language_provider.dart and referenced by NO UI (no picker). Writing flutter.app_locale_p1=he and relaunching left the UI in English (/tmp/he_home.png: 'Good evening','DASHBOARD','Streak' all still English).
findings.detail: The app UI locale resolves from the device locale (WidgetsBinding.window.locale via localeResolutionCallback) and the only exposed 'English/Hebrew' control is Calendar Preference (dates only), not UI language. There is no reachable control to switch the Progress screen UI to a Hebrew locale, and the per-profile app_locale pref did not switch it. Consequence: the he UI-LOCALE permutation could not be exercised here (Hebrew-SCRIPT via the Hebrew-Terms toggle WAS exercised and is correct). This is a coverage gap / possibly an unwired feature rather than a visual defect on Progress.

findings.title: Wizard unit pluralization: '11 Masechta' / '50 פרק' / '40 פרק' (singular unit with plural count)
findings.permutation: track-creation wizard reachable from Progress>per-track and Settings; en (Seder picker) and he (Chumash sefer picker)
findings.evidence: /tmp/wiz3.png 'Seder Moed — 11 Masechta'; /tmp/child_chumash.png 'בראשית — 50 פרק', 'שמות — 40 פרק'. Counts > 1 keep the singular unit word.
findings.detail: The count subtitle uses the singular unit noun regardless of count: '11 Masechta' should be the plural 'Masechtos' (ashkenazi) and '50 פרק' should be 'פרקים'. The oracle defines distinct plural unit words (Masechta/Masechtos, פרק/פרקים) so this is an incorrect-form (not just cosmetic) issue. Appears in the wizard which is reachable from the Progress per-track tile and Manage Tracks; Progress's own tree uses the correct prefixed singular ('Daf 2','דף ב') so the tree is fine.

findings.title: Profile cards overflow (RenderFlex 'BOTTOM OVERFLOWED BY 1.2 PIXELS') under font_scale 1.3 on the profile picker reached via app cold-start to LEARN
findings.permutation: font=1.3, profile picker (entry path to LEARN)
findings.detail: With font_scale=1.3, relaunching the app lands on the 'Who is learning?' profile picker. BOTH profile cards render the yellow/black striped Flutter overflow banner reading 'BOTTOM OVERFLOWED BY 1.2 PIXELS' beneath the 'Tap to switch' label, and the profile names are ellipsized to 'CloudUs...' and 'LoopChi...'. This is a hard render overflow (not just truncation). It is on the profile-selector rather than the LEARN body itself, but it is squarely on the navigation path into LEARN and is the most severe visual defect found. A text-only loop would never see the overflow stripe.

findings.title: Bottom-nav 'DASHBOARD' label truncated to 'DASHBOA...' under font_scale 1.3
findings.permutation: font=1.3, LEARN screen (shared bottom nav)
findings.detail: Under large text (font_scale 1.3) the bottom navigation 'DASHBOARD' tab label is ellipsized to 'DASHBOA...' while LEARN / PROGRESS / SETTINGS fit. The nav bar is shared by the LEARN screen and is visible from it. At font 1.0 the label renders in full (verified in /tmp/audit/back_to_browse.png), confirming this is a large-text-specific clip. Low severity (cosmetic, still tappable) but a real accessibility regression for users with large fonts.

findings.title: Completing one of two daily-task tiles (Chullin 41a + 41b) clears BOTH and shows '0 Items / All caught up' — only one was marked complete
findings.permutation: data=populated->complete, hebrew-terms=ON
findings.detail: Daily Tasks listed '2 Items' as two tiles: 'חולין דף מא עמוד א' (Chullin 41a) and 'חולין דף מא עמוד ב' (Chullin 41b). I opened tile 1, used 'Next daily task' to advance to tile 2 (this does NOT complete tile 1), then tapped 'Mark complete' on tile 2 only. A 'Marked complete' snackbar appeared and on returning the counter dropped 2->0 with the 'All caught up / No tasks remaining for today' empty state — i.e. tile 1 (amud א) also vanished without being explicitly completed. Streak correctly went 0->1 and Personal Best 0->1, so this may be intended daf-granular completion (both amudim = one daf), but the UI presents two separately-completable tiles and one action cleared both. Needs confirmation of intent; flagged P2 because it could mean an amud got silently marked learned. Counter binds to allDailyTasksProvider tasks.length in learning_screen.dart:296.

findings.title: Base word מ-ש-נ-ה transliterated three inconsistent ways on one Browse screen: 'Mishnayos/Mishnayot', 'Mishneh', and 'Mishna' (Mishna Berurah drops trailing -h)
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms=OFF, nusach=Ashkenazi AND Sephardi
findings.detail: In the Browse list, three works built on מ-ש-נ-ה render with inconsistent spelling on the SAME screen: 'Mishnayos' (Ashk) / 'Mishnayot' (Seph), 'Mishneh Torah', and 'Mishna Berurah'. 'Mishna Berurah' drops the trailing -h that 'Mishneh' keeps and that conventional usage uses ('Mishnah Berurah'). These are distinct proper nouns so it is borderline, but the missing -h on Mishna Berurah specifically is non-standard and the tri-fold spelling of the same root on one screen reads inconsistent. Low-confidence oracle nit.

findings.title: Deep breadcrumb chips truncate at the right edge in the Browse drill-down ('...› B' for Berakhot)
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms=OFF, font=1.3, Browse leaf
findings.detail: In the Browse Content drill-down, the breadcrumb chip bar 'Talmud Bavli › Seder Zeraim › Berakhot' truncates the final chip to just 'B' at the right edge. It IS a horizontally scrollable chip bar (prior chips remain), so this is expected horizontal-scroll truncation, but the last (current) crumb being the one cut off is mildly awkward UX. Cosmetic.

findings.title: Daily Tasks count ('5 Items') and dashboard 'TODAY DUE: 5' never decrement when a task is completed
findings.permutation: caught-up with 5 due, post-completion, font 1.0, terms ON+OFF
findings.detail: Completing a daily task removes it and pulls the next verse into the list, holding the count at a constant 5. The dashboard 'TODAY DUE' circle likewise stays 5 after a completion (only 'Lifetime' incremented 5->6->7). Net effect: a user who completes today's tasks NEVER sees the due count go down, so there is no sense of progress toward 'caught up' and no reachable empty/zero-due state by working through the list. Either the counter should decrement as tasks are completed, or the label needs to communicate 'rolling queue' semantics. The completion itself works correctly (Lifetime increments, verse is removed).

findings.title: Dashboard STATS panel shows hardcoded-looking '0' / '0 of 0 sections' during load instead of a skeleton
findings.permutation: transient loading frame on dashboard entry, font 1.0
findings.detail: On entering the dashboard the small stat cards correctly show '...' placeholder dots (a recognizable skeleton), but the large STATS panel renders real-looking zeros: OVERDUE 0, TODAY DUE 0, '0 / 0 sections — 9 curricula', 0%. These zeros are visually indistinguishable from a legitimate caught-up/empty state, so for ~1-2 seconds the user is told there is nothing due today and no curriculum progress before the real values (5 due, 5/70,033) pop in. The STATS panel should use a skeleton/spinner consistent with the cards rather than displaying 0s while loading.

findings.title: Mixed Hebrew-script / English on one row: dashboard stat labels read 'Streak' | 'סימונים' | 'Lifetime'
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms ON, adult mode, font 1.0
findings.detail: With Hebrew Terms ON, the middle stat label Hebraizes to 'סימונים' (siyumim) while the flanking labels stay English ('Streak', 'Lifetime'), producing a jarring 2-English-1-Hebrew row. The accessibility string '0 סימונים earned' literally interleaves Hebrew script inside an English sentence. This is driven by the (working) Hebrew-terms toggle, but the half-translated row is a consistency defect: either all three domain-facing labels should follow the toggle or none should. Same pattern appears in Settings ('שבת MODE', 'silenced and locked during שבת and Yom Tov' — Shabbos in Hebrew script but Yom Tov transliterated) — see /tmp/audit/settings.png.

findings.title: Breadcrumb verse identifier wraps to its own line, orphaning the gematriya letter (Hebrew mode)
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms ON, nusach n/a (script), font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: Each task card's breadcrump 'בראשית › פרק א › פסוק ו' does not fit on one line, so 'פסוק' stays on line 1 and the single gematriya verse letter wraps alone to line 2, visually detached from its label 'פסוק'. In the first screenshot the orphaned 'ו' even reads ambiguously as 'א' at a glance. The transliteration mode wraps more gracefully ('Pasuk 8' stays together — /tmp/audit/learn_translit.png), so this is specific to the Hebrew-script breadcrumb. Not clipped/overflowing, but the orphaned single character is poor and the design should keep 'פסוק <n>' together or shrink/ellipsize the leading crumbs.

findings.title: Bottom-nav 'DASHBOARD' label ellipsizes to 'DASHBOA...' at font scale 1.3
findings.permutation: font 1.3, any nusach/terms, scheduler (Learn) tab
findings.detail: At accessibility font scale 1.3 the first bottom-navigation label is truncated to 'DASHBOA...'. Only the longest label is affected; the others render fully. This is a clipped/ellipsized text instance per the rubric. Font scale was reset to 1.0 after testing.

findings.title: No reschedule / skip control exists on adult Daily Tasks rows
findings.permutation: caught-up with 5 due, adult mode, font 1.0
findings.detail: The audit brief lists 'reschedule/skip' as a control to exercise, but the adult Daily Tasks list exposes no such control: rows are tap-only (open the study detail), swipe-to-reveal does nothing, and long-press just opens the detail. Inside a task the only actions are 'Mark complete' and 'Next daily task' (advance without completing). If reschedule/skip is an intended capability it is absent on this surface; if not, this is informational. ('Next daily task' is the closest thing to a non-destructive skip.)

findings.title: Streak headline pluralization wrong: '0 day streak!' (and '5 day streak!') — should be 'days'
findings.permutation: data state: streak=0; font 1.0 and 1.3; Activity & points expanded
findings.detail: The StreakWidget headline renders '0 day streak!' directly above 'Best: 0 days'. The ICU 'other' plural branch in streakWidgetDayStreak (app_localizations_en.dart:3267) is hard-coded as '$count day streak!' (singular 'day'), so EVERY non-1 count is wrong: count=0 -> '0 day streak!', count=5 -> '5 day streak!'. English requires the plural 'days' for the 'other' category. The mismatch is visible side-by-side with the correctly-pluralized 'Best: 0 days'. The 'one' branch ('1 day streak!') is correct. Fix: 'other' should read '$count days streak!'.

findings.title: Rapid double-tap on dashboard flame chip stacks two duplicate My Achievements screens
findings.permutation: adversarial: rapid back-to-back taps on streak/flame chip (no settle)
findings.detail: The dashboard streak/flame chip onTap is `context.router.push(const GamificationRoute())` (dashboard_body.dart:305) with no re-entrancy guard or duplicate-route check. Two quick taps push the same GamificationScreen twice; the user must press Back twice to escape. Confirmed by probe: after a double-tap, the first Back press kept 'My Achievements' on screen and only the second Back returned to the dashboard. Points balance (250) was not corrupted by the probe.

findings.title: Empty-state copy uses legacy 'earn/unlock/ladder' framing that contradicts the spend-economy model
findings.permutation: data state: 0 configured rewards
findings.detail: Per DEC-32/R4o-C1 (documented in achievements_overview_provider.dart and reward_milestone_service.dart) the auto-unlock achievement ladder was REPLACED by a spend economy: rewards are priced spend-items redeemed against a debitable balance. Yet the Achievements screen still says '0 / 0 Rewards', 'No rewards earned yet. Keep learning!' and Pro Tip 'Keep learning on your tracks to climb the reward ladder.' 'Earned' and 'reward ladder' describe the removed auto-unlock model; in the spend economy rewards are configured by a parent and spent, not earned by climbing a threshold ladder. Copy is internally inconsistent with the implemented mechanic.

findings.title: Child has 250 points but zero rewards/prizes configured anywhere — points are inert, with cheerful 'doing great' messaging
findings.permutation: data state: 250 points, 0 configured milestones; cross-checked Redeem Prizes
findings.detail: This is the '0 rewards vs configured' symptom, RESOLVED as a true empty data state rather than a display-wiring bug. Both surfaces read the same source (RewardMilestoneService SharedPreferences key reward_milestones_config_v1_<profileId>) and both are empty — verified via run-as: the prefs file contains NO reward_milestones_config_v1_* key at all. So Achievements ('0/0 Rewards') and Redeem Prizes ('No prizes configured yet') agree. The UX gap: the child has accumulated 250 spendable points with nothing to redeem them on, while the Achievements card reassures 'Keep it up, you're doing great!' — there is literally nothing to achieve or spend on until a parent configures rewards. A '0/0' rewards goal with a positive balance is a dead end that the copy papers over.

findings.title: My Achievements cannot exercise nusach / curriculum-label rendering in the empty state (coverage gap, not a defect)
findings.permutation: nusach Ashkenazi; hebrew-terms ON/OFF; 0 achievement rows
findings.detail: Because no track has configured/enabled milestones, achievementsOverviewProvider produces zero rows and zero per-track filter chips, so the screen renders NO curriculum/track-tag domain terms. The nusach (Ashkenazi/Sephardi) and Hebrew-terms levers therefore have no rendered surface to change ON THIS SCREEN — the only domain term ('Rewards', 'siyumim') doesn't appear in the achievement list. I verified the Hebrew-terms lever DOES work on the adjacent counter row: flipping it OFF changed the dashboard/Progress siyumim tile from Hebrew 'סיומים' to Ashkenazi transliteration 'Siyumim' (correct -im plural), then restored to ON. Full nusach coverage of achievement track-tags requires a profile WITH configured per-track rewards, which I could not construct (needs parent PIN + reward config flow).

findings.title: Counter row mixes one Hebrew-script label ('סיומים') among English siblings — intended toggle behavior, NOT a bug
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms toggle ON
findings.detail: Recorded to pre-empt a false positive: on both the Progress hub and Dashboard the four-tile counter row shows 'Streak / סיומים / Lifetime / Points' — one Hebrew label among English. This looks like a half-translated UI but is the intended effect of the Hebrew Terms toggle (hebrew_terms_script_p0=true), which localizes only the configured DOMAIN terms (siyumim, chazara) to Hebrew script while generic UI nouns stay English. Confirmed by flipping the toggle (script changed) and the rubric exception ('unless intended'). No defect.

findings.title: Search does not match Ashkenazi transliteration ("shabbos" -> No results) even though it matches Sephardi ("shabbat")
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms ON, p0 variant=ashkenazi / p1=sephardi, font 1.0
findings.detail: In the ContentHierarchy search, typing the Ashkenazi transliteration of מסכת שבת — "shabbos" — returns "No results for 'shabbos'". Typing the Sephardi spelling "shabbat" (or even partial "shab") correctly returns the שבת masechta and its descendants. So the search index only carries the Sephardi transliteration alias, not the Ashkenazi one. The app supports an Ashkenazi nusach (p0 variant is ashkenazi; the Pronunciation control offers Ashkenazi), so an Ashkenazi-leaning user who searches "shabbos" / "taanis" gets a false-empty result for content that is present. Search must alias both nuschaos (and ideally the Hebrew script form).

findings.title: Ashkenazi nusach mapping is incomplete — Sephardi -ah forms ("Beitzah", "Rosh Hashanah") render next to correctly-Ashkenazified siblings ("Shabbos", "Taanis", "Succah") on one screen
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms OFF, nusach=Ashkenazi, font 1.0, Talmud Bavli > Seder Moed
findings.detail: Switching the Pronunciation control to Ashkenazi correctly flips Shabbat->Shabbos, Taanit->Taanis, Sukkah->Succah, Nakh->Nach, Tanakh->Tanach, Mishnayot->Mishnayos. But on the SAME Seder Moed masechta list, "Beitzah" and "Rosh Hashanah" keep their Sephardi -ah endings (strict Ashkenazi would be Beitzoh/Beitza and Rosh Hashono/Hashana). The result is two different nuschaos visibly mixed on one screen (Shabbos/Taanis/Succah in -os/-is alongside Beitzah/Rosh Hashanah in -ah). This is the classic 'same screen, two nuschaos' oracle violation: the Ashkenazi transliteration table has gaps and silently falls back to the Sephardi/neutral form for some masechtos.

findings.title: Breadcrumb omits the current Daf segment at the Amud-list level in transliteration mode
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms OFF, nusach=Ashkenazi, font 1.0, Shabbos > Daf 2 > [Amud a / Amud b]
findings.detail: When you drill Talmud Bavli > Seder Moed > Shabbos > Daf 2, the Amud-selection screen's chip breadcrumb stops at 'Shabbos' (rendered as an underlined link) and never shows the current 'Daf 2'. There is no active/terminal node — both visible non-chip segments are links. So the user on the Amud a/Amud b screen cannot tell from the breadcrumb which daf they are inside. The text-display header breadcrumb one level deeper DOES include 'Daf 2 > Amud a', and the Hebrew-script-mode amud list (reached via back from the pager) showed the daf, proving the hierarchy breadcrumb is under-reporting its leaf level on the direct-drill path.

findings.title: Deepest breadcrumb active segment is clipped ("דף ב" -> renders as "ב‏ף") at large text (font_scale 1.3) and is not recoverable by scrolling
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms ON, Sephardi, font 1.3, Talmud Bavli > מועד > שבת > דף ב
findings.detail: At font scale 1.3 the 4-segment hierarchy breadcrumb 'תלמוד בבלי(chip) > מועד > שבת > דף ב' overflows. The pinned curriculum chip ('תלמוד בבלי') consumes fixed width and the scrollable portion does not auto-scroll to fully reveal the active rightmost (RTL) segment, so the current 'דף ב' is clipped — the leading 'ד' is cut at the container edge and it reads 'ב‏ף'. A horizontal swipe on the breadcrumb does NOT scroll it, so the clipped text is unrecoverable. Note the contrast: the text-DISPLAY header breadcrumb wraps to two lines at 1.3 (handles large text correctly), but the hierarchy/chip breadcrumb clips — different overflow handling between the two breadcrumb components.

findings.title: First curriculum row icon (חומש / Chumash) renders as a gray disc with a washed-out/near-invisible glyph while all sibling rows have colored, legible book icons
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms ON & OFF, font 1.0, LEARN > Browse top of list
findings.detail: On the Browse curriculum list, every curriculum tile has a tinted circular icon with a clearly-colored open-book glyph (teal/green/blue/purple) EXCEPT the first item Chumash/חומש, whose icon is a flat light-gray disc with a barely-visible gray book outline. It reads as a disabled/placeholder state next to its vivid siblings, drawing the wrong attention to the first (and arguably most fundamental) curriculum. This reproduces in both Hebrew and transliteration modes, so it is a deterministic per-curriculum color assignment issue, not a transient frame.

findings.title: Review-count term 'chazaros' is hardcoded Ashkenazi and does NOT follow the Sephardi nusach setting, producing two nuschaos on one screen
findings.permutation: nusach:Sephardi x hebrew-terms:OFF (transliterated), data:populated
findings.detail: With Pronunciation=Sephardi, the level names correctly render Sephardi: 'Bereshit', 'Shemot', 'Vayikra' (-t endings). But the subtitle review-count label still reads '7 chazaros' / '0 chazaros' (-os, the ASHKENAZI form). Switching Pronunciation to Ashkenazi proves the term is hardcoded: the names change (Bereshit->Bereishis, Shemot->Shemos) but 'chazaros' stays identical in both modes. So in Sephardi mode the user sees Sephardi seder names alongside an Ashkenazi domain term on the same line/screen — a direct violation of the same-masechta/single-nusach oracle. Sephardi should read 'chazarot'.

findings.title: Duplicate 'Learn' stage label: expanded breakdown shows two identical 'Learn: N' columns instead of distinct stage names
findings.permutation: data:populated, hebrew-terms:OFF and ON, both fonts
findings.detail: Expanding any level/perek shows a four-stage row. The first TWO stage labels are both 'Learn:' (Hebrew: both 'לימוד'), each showing the same value (7). A SRS curriculum should have four DISTINCT stage names (e.g. Learn, Review 1, Review 2, Review 3 or similar). Two stages collapsing to the same label 'Learn' is a stage-name/mapping bug; it is reproduced on every populated and empty row (Learn:0 Learn:0 ...) and in both Hebrew-script and transliterated modes, so it is structural, not a one-off.

findings.title: Header 'N chazaros' contradicts the per-stage review counts ('Review 1: 0, Review 2: 0') — 'chazaros' (=reviews) is shown for items with zero reviews done
findings.permutation: data:populated, both nusach, both hebrew-terms states
findings.detail: The card subtitle says '7 chazaros' (chazara = review/repetition) while the same card's stage breakdown shows Review 1: 0 and Review 2: 0 — i.e. zero reviews were actually performed. The '7 chazaros' value tracks the Learn count (7 items learned), so the word 'chazaros' is being misused to mean total completions/sections rather than literal reviews. Lifetime Knowledge restates this as '7 items learned / 7 total chazaros'. Consistent app-wide but semantically wrong: calling never-reviewed learned items 'chazaros' is misleading domain terminology.

findings.title: Leaf pasuk status renders 'Live' — an opaque internal-looking enum value as the learner-facing completion state
findings.permutation: Lifetime Knowledge -> Bereishis -> Perek 1 -> pesukim, data:populated
findings.detail: Drilling to the leaf level, each learned pasuk (green dot, Pasuk 1-6) shows the right-aligned status 'Live'. 'Live' reads like an internal status enum (live/draft) rather than a meaningful learner completion state (Learned/Done/a date). For a verse a user has studied, 'Live' is ambiguous jargon with no legend; it looks like a developer value leaking into the UI. Not-yet-learned pesukim (7,8) correctly show no label.

findings.title: Overall Progress header is visually unbalanced: 'Track progress:' wraps awkwardly across 3 lines while 'Lifetime: 0%' sits alone with empty space
findings.permutation: all states; worse at font:1.3
findings.detail: The blue Overall Progress card's two headline stats are mismatched in layout: left column 'Track progress: 0%' breaks onto three lines ('Track' / 'progress:' / '0%') while right column 'Lifetime: 0%' stays one line with large empty space below it. At font_scale 1.3 it degrades further ('Lifetime:' / '0%' wraps too) but no clipping/overflow stripes occur. Cosmetic mis-alignment / poor two-up layout, not a hard break.

findings.title: Hebrew-terms ON shows Hebrew-script stat label 'סיומים' next to English 'Streak'/'Lifetime' on Dashboard/Progress stat cards (mixed-script row)
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms:ON, Dashboard + Progress header cards
findings.detail: With Hebrew Terms ON, the middle stat card label renders 'סיומים' (Hebrew script) while the flanking cards stay English 'Streak' and 'Lifetime'. Flipping Hebrew Terms OFF turns it into 'Siyumim' (so the toggle does drive it — expected). The residual issue is inconsistency: only the 'siyumim' term Hebraizes while the other two stat labels remain English, yielding a one-row mix of Hebrew-script and English chrome. Either all three stat labels should follow the toggle or none, for visual consistency.

findings.title: Level-counter row shows plural "siyumim" for count = 1 ("1 aggregate-level siyumim")
findings.permutation: populated grouped view, Hebrew-terms ON and OFF, font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: The top level-counters card renders "1 aggregate-level siyumim" with a count of 1 but the plural Hebrew noun "siyumim" (singular is "siyum"). The rubric flags count=1 pluralization as a defect; it should read "1 aggregate-level siyum". Root cause confirmed in source: learning_tracker/lib/l10n/app_en.arb lines 1907/1914/1921 — siyumimLevelCurriculum/siyumimLevelAggregate/siyumimLevelUnit are all defined as plain templates "{count} ...-level siyumim" with NO ICU plural ({count, plural, ...}) selector. So ALL THREE rows render "1 ... siyumim" whenever a tier has exactly 1. Reproduced live on the aggregate row (count 1). The other two rows would show the same bug at count 1.

findings.title: Aggregate seder label duplicates the level word: "Siyum Seder Seder Zeraim" (transliteration modes only)
findings.permutation: populated grouped + timeline; Hebrew-terms OFF; both Ashkenazi and Sephardi nusach
findings.detail: In transliteration mode (Hebrew-terms OFF, Ashkenazi OR Sephardi) the aggregate milestone renders "Siyum Seder Seder Zeraim" — the word "Seder" appears twice. In Hebrew-terms ON mode the same row reads correctly "סיום סדר זרעים" (one Seder). Root cause: the Bavli level-1 content key is stored WITH the level word ("Seder Zeraim" — confirmed in curriculum_scopes.scope_value), and aggregateSiyumLabel() in siyum_milestone_label.dart builds '${terms.siyumSeder} $aggregateName' = "Siyum Seder " + "Seder Zeraim". In Hebrew mode the renderer substitutes the bare Hebrew name "זרעים" (no prefix), avoiding the duplication; the transliteration path returns the raw key verbatim. The label code comment even claims aggregateName is e.g. 'Zeraim' (bare) — but the real stored key is "Seder Zeraim". Affects both grouped and timeline views (shared label builder), and persists across both nuschaos.

findings.title: Curriculum scope stores English translation "Genesis" instead of transliteration (Bereishis/Bereshit)
findings.permutation: data inspection of chumash track (KidTest); cross-checked against Pronunciation setting copy
findings.detail: The chumash learning-track scope is persisted as scope_value='Genesis' — the English translation of the sefer name. The domain oracle explicitly flags this: "Genesis is wrong; it's Bereishis/Bereshit". The app's own Pronunciation toggle copy uses the correct transliteration Bereishis/Bereshit, so the stored "Genesis" is inconsistent with the app's own naming convention. Did not surface a Siyum HaTorah row on this screen for that profile (KidTest has no chumash completions), but if a chumash sefer siyum were earned the standalone unit row would frame this raw value; the transliteration code path resolves via content keys, but the stored seed value is the translation, which is the oracle violation.

findings.title: Timeline month headers use hardcoded English month names, inconsistent with locale-formatted card dates
findings.permutation: populated timeline view, all nusach/terms/font permutations
findings.detail: The timeline groups milestones under month headers ("June 2026", "May 2026") produced by SiyumimTimelineView._monthKey(), which indexes a hardcoded English const months[] array — it never goes through DateFormat. The per-card date subtitles, by contrast, use formatMilestoneDate() => DateFormat.yMMMd(locale). This is an internal inconsistency: two date surfaces on the same screen format via different mechanisms, one locale-aware and one not. Currently masked because the UI locale is force-English (known MaterialApp locale:null bug), but it is a latent localization defect that would diverge the moment the locale bug is fixed.

findings.title: Aggregate subtitle reads "All 1 complete" (awkward count=1 phrasing)
findings.permutation: populated grouped view (Seder Zeraim aggregate contains a single masechta)
findings.detail: When an aggregate contains exactly one unit (Bavli Seder Zeraim has only Berakhos with gemara), the subtitle renders "All 1 complete · Jun 9, 2026". The template siyumimAggregateSubtitle has no plural handling, so count=1 yields the grammatically awkward "All 1 complete". Lower severity than the noun-pluralization issue because "complete" carries no number agreement, but it reads unnaturally for the single-unit seder case which is reachable in real Bavli data.

findings.title: Timeline represents a single completion twice as peer rows (unit Berakhos + its sole-member Seder Zeraim aggregate)
findings.permutation: populated timeline view
findings.detail: In timeline mode a single masechta completion (Berakhos, the only gemara masechta in Seder Zeraim) appears as BOTH a unit milestone (Siyum Masechta Berakhos) and an aggregate milestone (Siyum Seder Zeraim) on the same date — visually the one act of finishing Berakhos shows up twice as adjacent peer rows. The grouped view avoids this by nesting Berakhos inside the aggregate (absorbedUnitKeys). Code comments state timeline intentionally "flattens the hierarchy" so this is likely by-design, but for single-member aggregates it reads as duplicate/redundant celebration of one milestone and is worth a product decision. Logged as P2 exploration, not a hard bug.

findings.title: Saved notification preferences are NOT restored after app relaunch — screen reverts to all defaults
findings.permutation: profile=CloudUser; persisted {reminder=ON@22:00, streak=OFF, reward=OFF}; cold restart x3
findings.detail: Set Daily Reminder time to 10:00 PM and turned Streak Alert + Reward OFF. Verified persisted prefs on device: daily_reminder_hour_1=22, streak_alert_enabled_1=false, reward_notification_enabled_1=false (run-as cat FlutterSharedPreferences.xml). After force-stop + relaunch + re-select CloudUser + open Notifications, the screen displays ALL toggles ON and Reminder Time = 7:00 PM (the defaults). Reproduced across THREE separate cold restarts; prefs file confirmed UNCHANGED each time (still hour=22, streak=false, reward=false), so this is a load/restore defect, not a write or wipe. Accessibility dump cross-confirms: all Switch widgets checked=true, Reminder Time content-desc='7:00 PM'. Root cause is in learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart: ReminderEnabled/StreakAlertEnabled/RewardNotificationEnabled/ReminderTime/StreakAlertTime each return a hard-coded default ('return true' / 7PM/9PM) synchronously in build() and async-load from prefs under ref.watch(activeProfileIdProvider). activeProfileIdProvider returns the sentinel 0 while the profile resolves (active_profile_provider.dart: 'selected ?? 0'); _loadFromPrefs(0) reads non-existent *_0 keys → falls back to defaults, and the reload under the resolved real id (1) does not land in the displayed state. The in-code comments claim a prior fix ('Fixes the cold-start race where ref.read returned 0') but it is incomplete for the profile-selector → profile path. User impact: anyone who turns OFF streak/reward notifications or changes reminder time silently gets them reset to ON / 7PM on every restart — a real privacy/UX harm (unwanted notifications re-enable themselves).

findings.title: 'HOT STREAK' badge stays shown even when Streak Alert toggle is OFF
findings.permutation: Streak Alert toggled OFF, font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: The red 'HOT STREAK' badge in the Streak Alert card header is a static label (l10n.notifHotStreakBadge, hard-wired in notifications_screen.dart as trailingTopBadge) and remains fully visible/coloured even after the Streak Alert switch is turned OFF and the Streak Alert Time row is greyed out. A disabled feature still advertising an active-sounding 'HOT STREAK' status is misleading. Cosmetic but state-inconsistent.

findings.title: Daily Reminder & Streak Alert switches are not accessibility-labelled (NAF=true)
findings.permutation: any state
findings.detail: In the UI hierarchy, the Daily Reminder and Streak Alert Switch nodes have content-desc='' and NAF='true' (Not Accessibility Friendly); the descriptive text ('Daily Reminder / Don't forget to learn today!') lives only on the sibling container View, not on the focusable Switch itself. The Device notifications and Reward Notifications switches DO carry their own content-desc. A screen-reader user focusing the Daily Reminder / Streak Alert switch would hear an unlabeled toggle. Inconsistent and an a11y gap.

findings.title: CORE FLIP VERIFIED: curriculum terms re-render to the correct nusach/script variant
findings.permutation: nusach Ashkenazi↔Sephardi and hebrewTerms OFF→ON, font 1.0
findings.detail: Not a defect — positive confirmation the required behaviour works. On the SAME Chumash Reorder list, the five books re-rendered live and correctly with each lever: Ashkenazi = Bereishis / Shemos (heading 'Seferim'); Sephardi = Bereshit / Shemot (heading 'Sefarim'); Hebrew-terms ON = בראשית / שמות (heading חומשים, RTL). Variant-invariant books (Vayikra, Bamidbar, Devarim) correctly stayed identical across nuschaos. Oracle checks all pass: -os/-eis (Ashk) vs -ot/-eshit (Seph) correct; no same-masechta-in-two-nuschaos; no stray Hebrew-script chars in English mode; Shabbos↔Shabbat label on the Shabbos-mode card also follows the nusach lever.

findings.title: Hebrew-terms Switch has no accessibility label (NAF=true, empty content-desc)
findings.permutation: hebrewTerms control, any state
findings.detail: The Hebrew-terms toggle Switch is flagged Not-Accessibility-Friendly by uiautomator and exposes an empty content-desc, so a screen-reader user gets no label announcing what the switch controls (its title 'Hebrew Terms' is a sibling node, not associated as the switch's label). The Calendar/Pronunciation/Nikud segmented controls DO expose proper labels (English/Hebrew, Ashkenazi/Sephardi, etc.), making this toggle the odd one out. Accessibility/semantics gap, not a visual break.

findings.title: Inconsistent date localization on track-detail reached from curriculum settings: 'Started' is Hebrew gematriya but 'Since'/'Est. finish' stay Gregorian
findings.permutation: Calendar Preference = Hebrew, Chumash track detail
findings.detail: With Calendar Preference set to Hebrew, the 'Started' value renders as a Hebrew gematriya date (כ"ה סיוון תשפ"ו) — correct — but on the SAME screen 'Since Jun 10, 2026' and 'Est. finish Aug 21, 2029' render in Gregorian English. Two date formats on one screen under one calendar preference. The Hebrew-calendar setting is applied inconsistently (only some date fields honour it). Adjacent to the curriculum-settings controls (it's the curriculum/track surface those controls drive), not the controls screen itself.

findings.title: Redundant value text 'Elapsed 0 days' duplicates its own row label 'Elapsed'
findings.permutation: Chumash track detail, font 1.0
findings.detail: Row label is 'Elapsed' and the corresponding value reads 'Elapsed 0 days', so the word 'Elapsed' is shown twice in the same row. Minor awkward phrasing / label duplication; value should likely be just '0 days'.

findings.title: Bottom-nav 'DASHBOARD' clips to 'DASHBOA…' at font scale 1.3
findings.permutation: font=1.3, any settings sub-state
findings.detail: At large text (font_scale 1.3) the bottom navigation label 'DASHBOARD' is ellipsized to 'DASHBOA…' while LEARN/PROGRESS/SETTINGS fit. The curriculum-settings controls themselves (Calendar Preference, Hebrew Terms, Pronunciation, Nikud, Add Lifetime Learning) all wrap cleanly at 1.3 with no clipping/overflow — only the shared nav chrome clips. Reported because it is consistently visible on this screen at 1.3.

findings.title: Mixed-language screen title 'חומש • Reorder' in Hebrew-terms mode
findings.permutation: hebrewTerms=ON, Chumash Reorder
findings.detail: With Hebrew terms ON the curriculum term in the app-bar title renders Hebrew (חומש) while the action word stays English ('Reorder'), producing a half-translated title 'חומש • Reorder'. This is consistent with the KNOWN logged MaterialApp locale:null bug (UI chrome stays English) so it is expected rather than a new defect — recorded only so the reviewer can correlate it with that known issue. Also a minor RTL note: in Hebrew mode the list text right-aligns but the drag-handles stay on the right (list did not mirror), so handles now sit immediately left of the right-aligned term instead of the trailing edge.

findings.title: Pluralization bug: '1 Active days' (should be singular 'Active day')
findings.permutation: All Time tab; reproduced with Hebrew-Terms ON and OFF, and at font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: The All-time activity stat block renders 'Active days' with the count of 1 ('1 Active days'). For count==1 this must read 'Active day'. This is the rubric's '1 study days' pluralization defect and is independent of the terms/nusach levers. The adjacent 'done' stat is correctly invariant, so only the days-counter label needs a singular/plural form.

findings.title: Half-translated, mixed-direction stat label '1 לימוד done' when Hebrew Terms ON
findings.permutation: All Time tab, Hebrew-Terms ON
findings.detail: With Hebrew Terms ON the right-hand all-time stat is a single label that jams the RTL Hebrew domain word 'לימוד' (limud) next to the LTR English word 'done'. Because of bidi the rendered order reads visually as 'done לימוד', a confusing mixed-script / mixed-direction phrase. Toggling Hebrew Terms OFF produces a clean 'Limud done', confirming this is a half-translated composition: the verb 'done' is never localized and is concatenated to the (now Hebrew-script) noun. Should be a single fully-resolved phrase per terms mode.

findings.title: Half-translated UI: Progress stat-card row mixes English and Hebrew ('Streak' / 'סיומים' / 'Lifetime')
findings.permutation: Progress hub screen (entry to Recent Activity), Hebrew-Terms ON
findings.detail: On the Progress hub the three summary cards render 'Streak' (English), 'סיומים' (Hebrew script), 'Lifetime' (English) side by side. With Hebrew Terms ON only the middle (siyumim) label flips to Hebrew script while the flanking labels stay English, producing an inconsistent half-translated row. Either all domain labels in this row should respond to the terms toggle or none should.

findings.title: Streak headline contradicts calendar under a zero-activity curriculum filter
findings.permutation: Category filter = Mishna Berurah (no completions), Last 7 Days and Last 30 Days
findings.detail: Filtering to a curriculum with no activity (Mishna Berurah) leaves the big headline as '1 Day Streak', the red badge '1-day streak', and 'Personal Best: 1', while the calendar marks today (Wed 10) as a hollow/empty circle (not completed) and adds the subtitle 'Streak across all curricula'. A user reading the filtered view sees a claimed 1-day streak with no filled days, which is visually contradictory. The subtitle partially explains the global nature of the streak, but the headline/badge should either reflect the filter or be visually subordinated so it does not contradict the empty calendar.

findings.title: Empty filtered charts show no 'no data' placeholder
findings.permutation: Category filter = Mishna Berurah (no completions)
findings.detail: Under a zero-activity filter the Limud bar chart renders as a completely blank plot area (axis labels only, no bars, no message) and the Cumulative Progress line renders a flat baseline with a single isolated dot at the far right (value 0). There is no empty-state messaging (e.g. 'No activity in this range'). The lone trailing dot on a flat zero line is an odd rendering. Functional, not broken, but a friendlier empty state would avoid a 'blank/lingering' impression.

findings.title: Add-Track 'Join a Program' step: 'Starts:' field shows the program NAME instead of a start date
findings.permutation: Add Track wizard step 2 'Join a Program?', both Hebrew-terms ON and OFF
findings.detail: On the 'Join a Program?' step (reached via the hub's ADD TRACK CTA → select Talmud Bavli), the Dirshu program card has a calendar-icon row labelled 'Starts:' whose value is the program's own name, not a date. In transliteration mode it reads literally 'Starts: Dirshu Amud HaYomi' and in Hebrew-terms mode 'Starts: דרשו עמוד היומי'. This matches the rubric 'a name where a date belongs' — the start-date binding is wrong (the name is being substituted for the cycle/track start date). Adjacent cards ('Daf Yomi' → 'DAILY CALENDAR', 'Daf a Week') do NOT show a bogus date, so the defect is specific to the program-with-start-date card.

findings.title: Add-Track wizard step-count denominator is unstable and goes stale (1 OF 6 → 1 OF 7)
findings.permutation: Add Track wizard, first entry vs after advancing to a program-bearing step and pressing Back
findings.detail: The curriculum-select screen shows 'STEP 1 OF 6' on first entry. Selecting Talmud Bavli (which has programs) advances to 'STEP 2 OF 7' — the total silently grows from 6 to 7. Pressing Back returns to curriculum-select but it now reads 'STEP 1 OF 7' instead of reverting to 6. So the denominator is sticky/stale: the first step is mislabeled as 1-of-7 before any program is even chosen, and the displayed total retroactively changes based on a later selection. Confuses the user about flow length and makes the progress bar inconsistent.

findings.title: Track detail: redundant label — 'Elapsed' row value repeats the word ('Elapsed 0 days')
findings.permutation: Track detail (from hub), all term/nusach modes, font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: On the track detail stats card the left label is 'Elapsed' and the right-hand value is 'Elapsed 0 days', so the word 'Elapsed' is printed twice on the same line ('Elapsed: Elapsed 0 days'). The sibling rows are clean (label 'Started' → value, label 'Actual pace' → value). The value string should be just '0 days'. Persists at font 1.3.

findings.title: Delete/Archive dialog: destructive action is the most prominent button and the three actions are mis-aligned (staircase)
findings.permutation: Delete Track dialog (from track detail), font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: The 'Delete Track' dialog ('What should happen to your completion history?') stacks three actions: 'Cancel' (right-aligned text link), 'Archive (keep history)' (centred-ish text link), and 'Delete and wipe history' (large solid red filled button). Two issues: (1) Safety hierarchy is inverted — the irreversible 'Delete and wipe history' is the single most visually dominant element while the safe 'Cancel' is the least prominent. (2) The three buttons sit at three different horizontal offsets producing a ragged staircase rather than a consistent right-aligned or full-width stack. At font 1.3 the red button label wraps to two lines ('Delete and wipe' / 'history') left-justified inside the centred pill, which looks unpolished (no hard clipping/overflow, text stays readable).

findings.title: Track detail mixes two date systems for the same 'start' event (Hebrew date vs Gregorian)
findings.permutation: Track detail, Calendar Preference = Hebrew (default), Hebrew-terms ON and OFF
findings.detail: On one card the 'Started' row shows a Hebrew-script Hebrew date (כ"ה סיוון תשפ"ו) while a few rows down the same track shows 'Since Jun 10, 2026' (Gregorian, English). Both describe the track's start (today), yet they render in two different calendars and scripts on the same screen. In transliteration mode this is especially jarring: a transliterated English title ('Talmud Bavli') with a Hebrew-script date above and a Gregorian date below. Worth aligning to one representation or clearly differentiating the two fields.

findings.title: Archive/Delete dialog offers actions the app then silently refuses (last active curriculum)
findings.permutation: Delete Track dialog → Archive (keep history) on the only/last active track
findings.detail: With a single active track, the 'Delete Track' dialog still presents 'Archive (keep history)' and 'Delete and wipe history' as available. Tapping 'Archive (keep history)' does not archive — it dismisses and shows a snackbar: 'At least one curriculum must remain active — You cannot remove your last active curriculum. Add another curriculum before removing this one.' The guard itself is good, but the restriction is only surfaced AFTER the user commits in the destructive dialog; better UX would disable/annotate those options up front. Also note this guard makes the empty-active-tracks state effectively unreachable for an existing profile.

findings.title: Rapid-tap race: a 5th keypad tap leaks past the enter→confirm transition into the Confirm step as digit 1
findings.permutation: Set Parent PIN (setup) flow, child profile PinKid, font 1.0
findings.detail: On the 'Set Parent PIN' setup keypad I fired 5 concurrent taps on digit '1' with no settle. The first 4 completed the first-entry PIN '1111' and auto-advanced to 'Confirm New PIN' — but the screenshot shows the Confirm step already has ONE dot filled. The 5th physical tap, which the user intended as part of the first entry, bled through and became digit 1 of the confirm PIN. Root cause (verified in code): in lib/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/parent_pin_setup_dialog.dart _onFourDigits(), the enterNew→confirm transition does setState({_isConfirmStep=true; _digits=''}) WITHOUT setting _busy=true; the appendDigit guards are only `_busy` and `_digits.length>=4`. After the buffer resets to '' the next queued tap sees length 0 and appends. The identical gap exists in lib/features/profiles/presentation/providers/pin_flow_controller.dart _handleSetup/_handleChange (the synchronous step transitions never raise busy). Real-world impact: a fast or fat-fingered parent gets an unexplained leading digit in the confirm field → spurious 'PINs do not match', or in the worst ordering a confirm that silently includes an unintended digit. The verify-mode keypad does NOT exhibit this (its _onFourDigits sets busy=true synchronously before the async verify), so the bug is specific to the step-advancing setup/change flows.

findings.title: Partial parent-PIN entry survives backgrounding — masked digit persists across HOME/resume on the verify gate
findings.permutation: PIN-entry gate (verify), child profile RedeemKid, font 1.0
findings.detail: With one digit entered on the 'Enter Parent PIN' gate I pressed KEYCODE_HOME, then relaunched the app. The dialog is still open AND the one entered (masked) dot is still filled — the in-progress PIN was not cleared on pause. For a parent-control security gate, the expected hardening is to clear partial entry (or dismiss the prompt) when the app is backgrounded, so a child who picks up the device cannot resume a parent's half-typed PIN or read the entered-digit count. The dialog is barrierDismissible:false with PopScope canPop:false, so it also cannot be dismissed by the child via back — but the lingering partial entry is still a minor leak/UX concern. The digits are masked, so severity is P2.

findings.title: Change-PIN 'Enter Current PIN' step reuses the verify subtitle 'to access parent settings' (copy mismatch)
findings.permutation: Change PIN flow, verifyCurrent step, font 1.3
findings.detail: When opening Parental Controls → Parent PIN (which routes to the CHANGE flow because a PIN already exists), step 1 'Enter Current PIN' shows the subtitle 'Enter your 4-digit PIN to access parent settings.' This is the verify-gate subtitle (enterParentPinSubtitle), reused for the change flow's verifyCurrent step (see parent_pin_keypad_dialog.dart _subtitle: case verifyCurrent returns l10n.enterParentPinSubtitle). In a change context the user is not 'accessing parent settings' — they are confirming identity before changing the PIN, so the copy is slightly misleading. Cosmetic.

findings.title: Mixed-script curriculum labels on the dashboard while Hebrew-terms toggle is ON (Hebrew term beside English labels)
findings.permutation: Dashboard (ambient to pin_flow nav), Hebrew-terms ON, both child + adult profiles
findings.detail: Not part of the PIN dialogs themselves, but observed while navigating SETTINGS→Parental Controls. On the dashboard stats row the middle stat renders the Hebrew-script term 'סיומים' (siyumim) directly next to English labels 'Streak', 'Lifetime', 'Points', and the stats card mixes 'חזרה' (Hebrew) with English 'OVERDUE'/'TODAY DUE'. The uiautomator content-desc confirms: '0 סיומים earned … Streak … Lifetime … Points'. With the Hebrew-terms toggle ON this is the intended term rendering, but the single-screen mixing of Hebrew-script domain terms with English chrome labels reads as half-translated. Flagged for the domain oracle since the same screen shows two scripts. No nusach inconsistency was detected (no masechta rendered in two nuschaos).

findings.title: New profile created but header/active-profile context stayed on the previous profile during PIN setup
findings.permutation: Set Parent PIN setup, immediately after creating child profile PinKid
findings.detail: After 'Create Profile' for PinKid, the forced 'Set Parent PIN' dialog correctly names PinKid ('…parent controls for PinKid'), but the app-shell header chip behind the dialog still shows 'RedeemKid / CHILD MODE' (the previously-active profile). The PIN was correctly written to the new profile (later verified — see below), so functionally correct, but the stale header context during setup is mildly confusing about which profile is being configured. Minor.

findings.title: Raw FirestorePermissionDeniedException string leaked into user-facing Backup & Sync card
findings.permutation: all permutations (font 1.0 and 1.3, terms ON/OFF) — error is persistent
findings.detail: The Backup & Sync hero card on the Parent Settings landing renders a raw internal exception verbatim: 'Sync error: FirestorePermissionDeniedException: The caller does not have permission to execute the specified operation. (collection: completions), op: read caused by: [cloud_firestore/permission-denied] The caller does not have permission to execute the specified operation. Tap to retry'. This exposes the exception CLASS NAME (FirestorePermissionDeniedException), the internal Firestore collection name (completions), the operation (read), and the internal error code path ([cloud_firestore/permission-denied]) — all developer-facing. Confirmed in code: learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/sync_orchestrator.dart:959-961 sets `message = e.toString()` for any non-TimeoutException, and learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/presentation/widgets/backup_sync_section.dart:115-119 renders `l10n.backupSyncError(message)` directly. The exception's toString (firestore_permission_denied_exception.dart:32-37) produces exactly this string. Tapping 'Tap to retry' re-runs the pull and re-surfaces the same raw text (persistent, not transient). At font 1.3 it wraps to 3+ lines and is even more prominent. Needs a user-friendly mapped message (e.g. 'Cloud backup is temporarily unavailable. Tap to retry.').

findings.title: Inconsistent tile-title capitalization: 'Reward configuration' breaks the title-case pattern of its siblings
findings.permutation: font 1.0, all term states
findings.detail: On the Parent Settings landing every management tile uses Title Case ('Manage Tracks', 'Manage Goals', 'Point Configuration', 'Adjust Points', 'Pending Prizes', 'Add Lifetime Learning', 'Manage Tutors') EXCEPT 'Reward configuration' which has a lowercase 'c'. The sub-screen it opens is titled 'Reward Configuration' (capital C), so the landing tile label is also inconsistent with its own destination header. Cosmetic but visible side-by-side.

findings.title: 'Manage Tracks' and 'Manage Goals' are two distinct tiles that route to the identical screen
findings.permutation: font 1.0
findings.detail: The landing presents 'Manage Tracks' (subtitle 'Add, edit, or archive your child's tracks') and 'Manage Goals' (subtitle 'Set pace or deadline goals for each track') as two separate rows, but both push ParentTrackManagementRoute (confirmed parent_settings_screen.dart:172 and :193) — the same 'Tracks & Goals' screen, which shows no goal-setting affordance until you drill into an individual track. A parent tapping 'Manage Goals' expecting a goals UI lands on the track list with no obvious goal control on that screen (goal editing is behind track -> Edit Goal). Confusing dual entry.

findings.title: Adjust Points amount field accepts an unbounded value (no max cap)
findings.permutation: Adjust Points dialog, font 1.0
findings.detail: In the Adjust Points dialog, entering '999999999999' (12 digits) is accepted and the Apply button becomes enabled — there is no maximum-value or length cap on the amount. The digitsOnly formatter correctly strips letters ('abc999999999999' -> '999999999999'), but a parent could add/deduct a nonsensical 999-billion-point adjustment in one tap. parent_settings_screen.dart only validates `amount > 0`. Low-severity robustness gap; a sane upper bound (and possibly a confirmation for very large values) would prevent accidental balance corruption.

findings.title: Mixed calendar systems on the track-detail screen (Hebrew date and Gregorian date together)
findings.permutation: Hebrew Terms ON + Calendar Preference = Hebrew, reached via Manage Tracks/Goals -> track
findings.detail: On the track-detail screen (two levels below the parent_settings landing, via Manage Tracks/Goals -> Chumash track) the 'Started' field renders a Hebrew gematriya date 'כ"ה סיון תשפ"ו' while the card immediately below shows 'Since Jun 10, 2026' (Gregorian) and 'Est. finish Apr 13, 2027' (Gregorian) — two different calendar systems on one screen for effectively the same anchor date. Inconsistent calendar presentation. Outside the strict landing scope but reachable from a parent_settings tile.

findings.title: "Archive (keep history)" destroys the track's goal/pace/program config but leaves the track active
findings.permutation: populated track, Sephardi, hebrew-terms OFF, font 1.3 (state-independent)
findings.detail: Long-pressed the child's Mishnayot track -> dialog -> tapped 'Archive (keep history)'. The list immediately showed 'No active tracks' (empty), but after any rebuild/refetch (font change OR navigate-away-and-back) the SAME track reappears as active with 1 RUNNING. Comparing TrackDetail before vs after archive: before had 'Required pace 21·Per week', 'Goal 21·Per week', 'Est. finish Apr 8 2030' and action 'Edit Goal'; after archive those Goal/Required-pace/Est-finish rows are GONE, subtitle degraded from 'Completion (with Chazara)' to generic 'Track progress', and the action tile flipped from 'Edit Goal' to 'Set Goal'. So 'Archive (keep history)' wiped the goal/program/completion-mode config (the opposite of 'keep history') yet did NOT remove the track from the active list. Source: parent_track_management_screen.dart _showDeleteDialog -> choice=='archive' calls dao.deleteTrackAndData(track.id) then invalidateAfterTrackDataChange; net observed effect is partial-delete + stale empty render. Data-integrity issue on a child's record managed by a parent.

findings.title: "Starts:" chip shows the program NAME instead of a start date
findings.permutation: Add Track flow Step 2 (Join a Program?), both nusach settings
findings.detail: On the 'Join a Program?' step reached from the Add Track control, the Mishnah Yomis card shows a calendar-icon chip reading 'Starts: Mishnah Yomis' — the field labeled 'Starts:' is followed by the program name, not a date. Confirmed in source program_selection_step.dart line 227: \"'Starts: \$name'\" interpolates the program name into the Starts label. A name where a date belongs (rubric: nonsense value).

findings.title: Empty-state and Delete dialog use own-profile copy ("your") in a parent-manages-child context
findings.permutation: empty state + delete dialog, all permutations
findings.detail: This screen is the PARENT managing the CHILD's tracks (the hub tile that opens it correctly says 'Add, edit, or archive your child’s tracks'). But the destination empty-state subtitle reuses l10n.manageTracksDetail = 'Create and edit YOUR learning tracks', and the archive/wipe dialog body says 'What should happen to YOUR completion history?'. Both leak the adult/own-profile wording into the child-management surface; should read 'your child’s'.

findings.title: Program-selection card name ignores nusach: "Mishnah Yomis"/"mishnayos" stay Ashkenazi-mixed even under Sephardi
findings.permutation: Add Track Step 2, hebrew-terms OFF, Sephardi (and ON)
findings.detail: With Pronunciation explicitly set to Sephardi, the curriculum picker correctly renders 'Mishnayot' (-ot) and the track card renders 'Mishnayot', but the program card on the SAME flow shows 'Mishnah Yomis' (Sephardi 'Mishnah' + Ashkenazi 'Yomis') and body 'Two mishnayos per day' (Ashkenazi -os). So one screen mixes nuschaos for the same masechta and the program name/description do not honor the user's nusach. The second program ('Perek Yomi' / 'פרק יומי') DOES respect the hebrew-terms toggle, making the first card's hardcoding inconsistent.

findings.title: Track-card subtitle and percent collide at large text ("Chazara)0%")
findings.permutation: populated, font_scale 1.3, hebrew-terms OFF
findings.detail: At font_scale 1.3 the track card's subtitle 'Completion (with Chazara)' expands until it touches the trailing '0%' value with no spacing, rendering as 'Completion (with Chazara)0%'. At 1.0 the gap is correct. Spacing/overflow robustness issue under accessibility text scaling (no Row spacing/Flexible between label and value).

findings.title: TrackDetail mixes Hebrew and Gregorian dates on one screen despite Hebrew calendar preference
findings.permutation: TrackDetail (reached from card), calendar pref = Hebrew
findings.detail: Calendar Preference is set to Hebrew. On the track detail the 'Started' date renders in Hebrew gematriya ('כ״ה סיוון תשפ״ו') but 'Since Jun 10, 2026' and 'Est. finish: Apr 8, 2030' render in Gregorian English on the same screen. Date formatting is inconsistent — some fields honor the Hebrew calendar preference, others ignore it.

findings.title: Duplicated label: "Elapsed" row renders the word twice ("Elapsed | Elapsed 0 days")
findings.permutation: TrackDetail, all permutations
findings.detail: The track-info Elapsed row uses label = l10n.trackInfoElapsed ('Elapsed') AND a value builder _elapsedRemainingLabel that ALSO prepends l10n.trackInfoElapsed, producing value 'Elapsed 0 days'. Net rendered row: 'Elapsed' (label) + 'Elapsed 0 days' (value) — the word 'Elapsed' appears twice. Value should be just '0 days'.

findings.title: Persistent mixed-language label "Completion (with חזרה)" on the track card
findings.permutation: populated, hebrew-terms ON, font 1.0
findings.detail: With hebrew-terms ON the track-card subtitle reads 'Completion (with חזרה)' — English 'Completion (with' + Hebrew-script 'חזרה)' on one line. Half-translated label (English chrome with a single Hebrew term embedded). Same pattern recurs on the goal tile ('משניות Per week') and the deadline preview ('About 4192 משניות per study day').

findings.title: Pluralization + absurd-magnitude in deadline preview: "4192 ... per study day, across 1 study days"
findings.permutation: Add Track Step 6 (goal/deadline), hebrew-terms ON
findings.detail: The disabled 'Set Deadline' card preview (accessibility text) reads: 'About 4192 משניות per study day, across 1 study days to finish the scope by the deadline (≈4192 items).' Two issues: (1) pluralization bug 'across 1 study days' should be '1 study day'; (2) magnitude is nonsensical — 4192 mishnayot per day across a single day (the full Shas-Mishnayot scope crammed into one day) because the deadline math divides the entire 4192-item scope by ~1 elapsed day. Also mixes 'משניות' (Hebrew) with English.

findings.title: "Manage Goals" hub tile lands on the same Tracks screen, not a goals view
findings.permutation: Parent Settings hub navigation
findings.detail: Parent Settings shows two distinct tiles with different subtitles: 'Manage Tracks' (Add, edit, or archive your child’s tracks) and 'Manage Goals' (Set pace or deadline goals for each track). Both navigate to the identical ParentTrackManagementRoute ('Tracks & Goals') with no goal-specific landing — to edit a goal the user must tap into a track card and find 'Edit Goal'. 'Manage Goals' arriving at a Tracks list is a navigation-expectation mismatch (the code comment at the title acknowledges the dual entry).

findings.title: Destructive 'Delete and wipe history' is the most visually prominent action; safe 'Archive' is a plain link
findings.permutation: delete/archive dialog, font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: In the 'Delete Track' dialog the destructive 'Delete and wipe history' is a large red filled button (highest visual weight) while the safer 'Archive (keep history)' and 'Cancel' are plain text links. The actions are also staggered/left-misaligned (right-aligned text buttons stacked above a wider centered red button). For an irreversible child-data-wipe, the destructive option drawing the eye is a UX risk.

findings.title: Pluralization wrong at value 1: shows "1 PTS" (plural) instead of singular
findings.permutation: value=1, hebrew-terms ON and OFF, font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: With points-per-task set to 1, both the large display and stepper render "1 PTS" — the plural unit. Singular should be "1 PT" or "1 point". Root cause: l10n key is a static count-independent string `pointSettingsPts => 'PTS'` (lib/l10n/app_localizations_en.dart:1429); there is no plural variant. The screen-reader content-desc also announces "1 / PTS" (confirmed via uiautomator dump), so the bug also reaches accessibility. The rubric explicitly flags count=1 pluralization. Reproduced cleanly at value 1; correct (plural) at 10/21/111.

findings.title: Stage label uses English translation "Learn" instead of transliteration "Limud" (Hebrew-terms OFF)
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms OFF, nusach Ashkenazi
findings.detail: When Hebrew Terms is OFF the stage descriptor renders "Learn · First completion (daily task)". "Learn" is the English TRANSLATION; the canonical transliteration for stage 1 is "Limud" (the codebase's own B1 vocabulary defines it: lib/core/labels/domain_term_labels.dart:232 `String get limud => _useHebrew ? 'לימוד' : 'Limud';`, and the comment at line 222 lists the English-default transliterated forms as "Siyum, Chazara, Limud"). The competing legacy map hardcodes the translation: lib/core/constants/hebrew_terms.dart:28 `'Learn': 'לימוד'` and line 71 `stageLearnEn = 'Learn'`. resolveStoredStageName (domain_term_labels.dart:191) returns the stored legacy English "Learn" verbatim instead of normalizing to "Limud". The rubric: labels must use transliteration, never the English translation. Curriculum name "Chumash" is correctly transliterated; only the stage word is wrong.

findings.title: Mixed-script line when Hebrew Terms ON: Hebrew stage term + English descriptor on one line
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms ON
findings.detail: With Hebrew Terms ON the subtitle renders "לימוד · First completion (daily task)" — a single line mixing Hebrew-script domain term with an English UI descriptor (pointSettingsPrimaryStageLabel stays English). The stage term flips to Hebrew but the suffix does not, producing a half-translated line. Arguably by-design (descriptor is UI chrome, not a domain term), but it reads as inconsistent on a screen whose other domain labels (חומש) are fully Hebrew.

findings.title: Blank body + green-square paint artifact for ~1-3s after background/resume
findings.permutation: populated, background(KEYCODE_HOME) then resume
findings.detail: After KEYCODE_HOME then relaunch, the Point Settings app bar restores immediately but the entire body (hero header, curriculum card, Save bar) is GONE — empty grey with a tiny green square artifact at screen center. Content self-heals after ~1-3s (autoDispose FutureProvider re-fetches, showing a transient empty/loading frame with a stray paint glitch). Visible flash of empty state + render artifact on every resume. Self-recovers, so P2, but a clean transition should keep the loading spinner or last content, not flash blank with an artifact.

findings.title: Context badge mismatch: header reads "CHILD MODE" on the parent-only Point Settings surface
findings.permutation: all (in-parent-mode under child profile RedeemKid)
findings.detail: Throughout the PIN-gated Point Configuration (a parent-only control surface, profile card shows a "PARENT" badge), the top app chrome still shows the child's name ("RedeemKid") with a "CHILD MODE" pill. The green "Parent mode — viewing RedeemKid" banner only appears on the settings list, not inside Point Config. A parent deep in admin controls sees a "CHILD MODE" badge — mode/context confusion (rubric: wrong account/mode for the context; parent-only surface under a child badge).

findings.title: Back-button with unsaved pending edit silently discards (no confirm dialog)
findings.permutation: populated, value bumped to 111 then KEYCODE_BACK
