findings.detail: Bumped points 1->111 (unsaved), pressed Back. It navigated straight to Parent Settings with no "Discard changes?" prompt; the pending edit was dropped silently. Re-entering confirmed the persisted value was unchanged (still the prior saved value). Low data-loss risk since save is explicit, but a parent who edits then hits Back loses the change with zero warning.

findings.title: Stepper +/- buttons expose no accessibility semantics (no labels, not seen as buttons)
findings.permutation: all
findings.detail: The increment/decrement controls are bare InkWell/Material with no Semantics label, so uiautomator (and screen readers) see them only as part of the merged card node — no actionable, labeled "Increase points"/"Decrease points" buttons. The whole card collapses into one content-desc string. A11y users cannot identify or operate the steppers. (Functional taps work fine for sighted users.)

findings.title: Preview pluralization wrong: a 1-point reward renders "1 Points"
findings.permutation: cost=1, font 1.0 (and 1.3)
findings.detail: With cost=1 the PREVIEW card reads "1 Points" — grammatically wrong, should read "1 Point". Root cause confirmed in source: lib/l10n/app_en.arb key rewardConfigPointsPreview = "{points} Points" is a plain int placeholder with NO ICU plural (=1{Point} other{Points}). Used in reward_configuration_screen.dart line 553 (_RewardPreview). The empty-form default also shows the nonsensical "0 Points". Any reward priced at exactly 1 point will display "1 Points" to the parent (and, since the same milestone data feeds the child Achievements surface, likely downstream too).

findings.title: "CHILD MODE" badge shown on a parent-only configuration surface
findings.permutation: all states (parent authenticated, viewing KidTest)
findings.detail: The persistent top bar shows avatar "K KidTest" with a blue "CHILD MODE" pill in the top-right corner across the entire Reward Configuration flow — a parent-only screen reached via Parent Settings after PIN. The same KidTest profile is simultaneously labelled "PARENT" on the Parent Settings card (rc_14/rc_40) yet "CHILD MODE" in the global bar. Mixed/contradictory mode indicators on a parent-restricted surface are confusing and look like a wrong-context badge. (Note: green system banner separately reads "Parent mode — viewing KidTest", a third mode label on screen.)

findings.title: Screen header still says "Configure New Reward" while editing an existing reward
findings.permutation: edit-existing-reward mode
findings.detail: Tapping the edit (pencil) icon on a reward in the Manage-rewards sheet loads that reward into the form, but the card heading remains "Configure New Reward", the subtitle remains the new-reward copy, and the button remains "Save Reward". Nothing on the form indicates edit vs create mode (only the post-save dialog differentiates "Reward updated" vs "Reward created", rc_28_updated.png). A parent who opens edit then gets distracted has no on-screen cue they are mutating an existing reward rather than adding a new one.

findings.title: Save with empty name gives zero feedback; Save button never disabled
findings.permutation: name empty + cost=5
findings.detail: The "Save Reward" button is always rendered enabled (navy, full opacity) regardless of validity. Tapping it with an empty name returns RewardSaveInvalidInput which the screen handles as a silent break/no-op (reward_configuration_screen.dart line 215-217, with code comment "button should be disabled" — but it is not). The user receives no explanation for why nothing happened. Same dead-end applies to cost=0/empty. Either disable the button until name+cost are valid, or surface an inline validation message.

findings.title: Empty-state copy "Tap below to add one" points at a button that does not exist in the sheet
findings.permutation: data: empty list (no rewards)
findings.detail: The Manage-rewards bottom sheet empty state (l10n rewardConfigEmptyMilestones) instructs "Tap below to add one." but the sheet contains no add button — the add-reward form lives on the screen BEHIND the sheet. There is nothing below the message to tap. The instruction is misleading; the user must dismiss the sheet to reach the form.

findings.title: Legacy milestone/threshold wording on a spend-economy reward ("Points needed", "reach the points goal")
findings.permutation: data: 1-2 rewards; save-confirmation dialog
findings.detail: Per the controller's own design note (reward_config_controller.dart lines 60-64: "every reward is now a single global priced spend-item redeemed against the one debitable balance"), rewards are PRICED items the child SPENDS points to redeem — not milestones the child REACHES. Yet the Manage list subtitle says "Points needed: N" (manage_rewards_list.dart line 114, key rewardConfigPointsThresholdLabel) and the created/updated dialogs say the child sees it "locked and blurred until they reach the points goal". "Needed/reach/goal" framing contradicts the redeem/spend model and will mislead parents about how the reward economy works.

findings.title: Rewards are de-duplicated by price, blocking two differently-named rewards at the same cost
findings.permutation: two rewards, same cost=1
findings.detail: saveReward() rejects any reward whose cost equals an existing reward's cost (_hasDuplicateThreshold, controller lines 132-142). In a spend economy this is a real limitation: a parent cannot offer two distinct prizes (e.g. "Ice Cream" and "Sticker") at the same price. The uniqueness-by-threshold constraint is a holdover from the old single-ladder milestone model where each rung had a distinct threshold; it does not fit priced redeemable items and silently caps the catalog the parent can build.

findings.title: Cost field accepts an unbounded value (9,999,999,999) with no upper cap
findings.permutation: cost=9999999999, huge name
findings.detail: The cost TextField only applies FilteringTextInputFormatter.digitsOnly (screen line 391) — no maxLength and no max-value validation. A 10-digit, ~10-billion-point price is accepted and previewed. There is no sane upper bound, so a reward can be made effectively unredeemable by typo, and the long name field likewise has no maxLength (a 70-char name was accepted, rc_35). Consider clamping cost to a reasonable maximum and capping name length.

findings.title: Weekday toggle UI (study/review selectors) is UNREACHABLE — no track is both self-paced and multi-stage
findings.permutation: Adult CloudUser/bavli (multi-stage, program-enrolled) and child LoopChild/mishnayos (self-paced, single-stage)
findings.detail: The full StudyDayConfig UI (Sun/Mon/.../Sat tiles, Study vs Review-only legend+badges, '$n study days per week' summary) only renders when trackHasChazara (stage count > 1) — confirmed in study_day_config_screen.dart:44-94. The ONLY multi-stage track in the device data is profile 1's 'bavli' (3 stages: לימוד/חזרה א׳/חזרה ב׳), but it has a profile_programs enrollment (program_id 5, 'Chullin 41'), and track_detail_screen.dart:582 gates the Study Days tile behind !hasProgramEnrollment — so its Study Days tile is HIDDEN (track detail shows only Set Goal / Edit Track / Delete Track). The only track that exposes Study Days is the child's single-stage 'mishnayos', which therefore hits the learn-only fallback. Net: the weekday toggles + study/review selectors + Save cannot be exercised live in this build state. DB-confirmed via curriculum_tracks (2 rows), stage_definitions (track 1 = 3 stages, track 2 = 0), profile_programs (bavli enrolled).

findings.title: Saturday is hardcoded 'Sat' — no Shabbos/Shabbat term, and day labels ignore Nusach + Hebrew-Terms toggles
findings.permutation: Weekday toggle grid (would render only for a self-paced multi-stage track); verified by code, not visually reachable
findings.detail: The study-day picker labels Saturday as generic 'Sat' via a const map with zero Nusach/Hebrew-Terms awareness. Every OTHER domain term in the app correctly flips with the Nusach control — I proved this live: flipping the child to Ashkenazi changed the lock banner from 'SHABBAT MODE / during Shabbat' to 'SHABBOS MODE / during Shabbos', and 'Mishnayot'→'Mishnayos', 'Berakhot'→'Berakhos'. The Study Days weekday row would still say 'Sat' (never Shabbos/Shabbat) and would not switch to Hebrew day names when Hebrew-Terms is ON. This is the exact 'Shabbos term' gap the audit targets. Marked P1 because it is a real, code-confirmed domain defect on the audited screen; could not be photographed because the state is unreachable (see blocked).

findings.title: Pluralization is CORRECT for count=1 ('1 study day per week') — verified clean, no '1 study days' bug
findings.permutation: Weekday summary line (code-verified; not visually reachable)
findings.detail: The summary correctly singularizes: studyCount==1 yields 'study day', otherwise 'study days'. No '1 study days' defect exists on this screen. Reported as an explicit clean result for the pluralization rubric item the audit calls out.

findings.title: Reachable Study Days screen renders a near-empty void with a single bare sentence
findings.permutation: Child LoopChild / mishnayos / learn-only fallback (Sephardi, Hebrew-Terms OFF, font 1.0)
findings.detail: The only reachable StudyDayConfig state shows just 'All days are study days for this track.' centered in a large blank screen, with no icon, illustration, or framing. No clipping, no overflow, good contrast, correct Nusach-aware title ('Mishnayot Study Days'). Not a rendering defect per se — it is the intended fallback (study_day_config_screen.dart:81-94) — but it reads as unfinished/empty for a top-level destination. P2 polish.

findings.title: Same six sedarim render in two different forms (Hebrew script vs Sephardi transliteration) across tracks under identical settings
findings.permutation: Adult CloudUser, Hebrew-Terms ON: bavli browse vs mishnayot browse (and child mishnayot under Sephardi)
findings.detail: The identical Shisha Sidrei list renders as Hebrew script for the Bavli track but as Latin Sephardi transliteration (Seder Tahorot, Seder Kodashim) for the Mishnayot track. This is adjacent to the audited screen (the Study Days title uses the same curriculumLabelText path). Because the screens differ by profile/track the two forms are not on one screen simultaneously, but it signals the Hebrew-Terms/Nusach term rendering is applied inconsistently per track — worth flagging since the Study Days title depends on the same label system.

findings.title: Reorder PERSISTS across full relaunch (verified at storage layer)
findings.permutation: Ashkenazi / hebrew-terms OFF / font 1.0 / populated
findings.detail: Dragged Devarim (last) to the top. UI updated to Devarim/Bereishis/Shemos/Vayikra/Bamidbar. Force-stopped com.jcom.torah.learning_tracker and relaunched; the profile picker re-appeared (parent session reset). Inspected the persisted per-account SQLite DB: track_learning_order for track_id=2 holds sefaria_ref/sort_order = Deuteronomy(0), Genesis(1), Exodus(2), Leviticus(3), Numbers(4) — i.e. Devarim first — exactly matching the post-drag order. This is a POSITIVE confirmation (the control works), recorded as P2 informational since the task explicitly required verifying persistence across relaunch.

findings.title: Storage key for ordered items is the Sefaria English book name, not a transliteration
findings.permutation: Ashkenazi / hebrew-terms OFF / font 1.0 / populated
findings.detail: The persisted sefaria_ref column stores raw Sefaria English book identifiers (Genesis/Exodus/Deuteronomy). On screen these are correctly rendered as transliteration via CurriculumLabel.local (Bereishis/Shemos/Devarim), so this is NOT user-visible — it is a stable ref-key by design. Flagged only so the next auditor does not mistake the DB string for a UI leak; the oracle rule ('Genesis is wrong, it's Bereishis') applies to UI labels/toasts, and the UI passes. No user-facing defect.

findings.title: Nusach (Ashkenazi/Sephardi) lever correctly drives curriculum term rendering
findings.permutation: Sephardi vs Ashkenazi / hebrew-terms OFF / font 1.0
findings.detail: On the reorder screen (Ashkenazi default) the 5 Seferim render with -os/-oh (Bereishis, Shemos) — correct Ashkenazi nusach, internally consistent, no Hebrew-script characters, no English translations. Flipping Pronunciation to Sephardi via child Settings changes the shared label path: the LEARN tab's Daily Tasks switched 'Bereishis' -> 'Bereshit' (-t Sephardi spelling). The reorder rows use the identical CurriculumLabel.local widget, so they inherit the same correct switch. Toggle is symmetric (restored to Ashkenazi cleanly). Positive result.

findings.title: Reorder applied silently with no confirm dialog (overdueCount=0) — expected, not a bug
findings.permutation: Ashkenazi / font 1.0 / track at 0%, 0 overdue
findings.detail: Per code, the reorder-amnesty ReorderConfirmDialog only appears when overdueCount > 0. The Chumash track is freshly started (0%, OVERDUE=0 on dashboard), so the drag committed immediately with no confirmation prompt and no visible toast/snackbar. Behavior matches intent. Noted so it is not mistaken for a missing-feedback defect; the save is optimistic + async with no success affordance, which is a deliberate design choice here.

findings.title: Reorder screen renders cleanly — no clipping, overflow, contrast, or alignment defects
findings.permutation: Ashkenazi / hebrew-terms OFF / font 1.0 / populated
findings.detail: Full-resolution crop inspection of the 5 rows and section header: section header 'Seferim' and labels Bereishis/Shemos/Vayikra/Bamidbar/Devarim are fully shown (no ellipsis, no mid-word break, no overflow stripes). Drag-handle glyphs (Icons.drag_handle) render as proper two-bar icons (not blank discs), right-aligned and consistently positioned, good contrast on light background. AppBar title 'Chumash • Reorder' intact; reset/refresh action icon present top-right. No overlapping/colliding tap targets. Clean.

findings.title: Parent-only Pending Prizes surface wears a 'CHILD MODE' badge and the child's name/avatar in the top bar
findings.permutation: populated + empty, font 1.0 and 1.3, Hebrew-terms ON
findings.detail: The persistent top ProfileSwitcherBar derives its role badge purely from activeProfile.profileMode (app_shell.dart ~line 437: activeProfile?.profileMode == ProfileMode.child -> l10n.profileBadgeChildMode). When a parent PIN-elevates to manage the child, the active profile is STILL the child (KidTest), and the green 'Parent mode — viewing KidTest' banner only renders on the main tab views, NOT on pushed sub-routes. Result: the Pending Prizes screen — a parent-only approve/decline surface — shows 'CHILD MODE' + child avatar 'KidTest' with no parent-mode disambiguation. On the Parent Settings screen the contradiction is on ONE screen: the inline profile card reads 'KidTest PARENT' while the top bar simultaneously reads 'CHILD MODE'. This matches the rubric's 'parent-only surface under a child badge' / 'wrong mode for the context'. Reproducible on every parent management sub-route.

findings.title: Pending Prizes empty state is bare centered text with no icon or illustration
findings.permutation: empty state, font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: The empty state (parent_pending_redemptions_screen.dart lines 85-97) renders only 'No pending prize requests.' as centered #6B7280 bodyMedium text on a large blank canvas — no icon, illustration, or supporting copy. Legible and contrast is fine, but it reads as an unstyled placeholder rather than a designed empty state, inconsistent with the polished card UI used when populated. Polish gap, not a defect.

findings.title: 'Decline' (refund/reject) is a low-emphasis gray text button, visually detached from Fulfil
findings.permutation: populated row, font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: On each card the primary 'Fulfil' is a filled navy button while 'Decline' is a low-emphasis #6B7280 gray TextButton sitting below and slightly detached to the lower-right with significant surrounding whitespace (parent_pending_redemptions_screen.dart lines 266-283). #6B7280 on white is ~4.8:1 (passes AA for normal text but borderline). For an action that spends/declines and triggers a point refund, the gray text treatment is a weak affordance and the floating placement weakens the visual pairing with Fulfil.

findings.title: Reward title in card uses Expanded Text with no maxLines/overflow (latent — not reproduced on this device)
findings.permutation: long title 'Extra Big Chocolate Fudge Sundae With Sprinkles And Cherry' @ font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: redemption.rewardTitle (lines 222-227) is rendered inside an Expanded Column with no maxLines or overflow:ellipsis. On this 2560px-wide tablet the long multi-word title fit on a single line even at font_scale 1.3, so NO clipping/overflow was visible (clean). Flagged as a latent risk only: on a narrow phone viewport or with an even longer title the unbounded title would wrap and grow the row height, potentially crowding the right-aligned Fulfil/Decline column. Could not visually reproduce a defect on this device — low confidence.

findings.title: Parent-only Manage Tutors surface renders under a 'CHILD MODE' badge
findings.permutation: parent mode (PIN-elevated) on child LoopChild, font 1.0 + 1.3
findings.detail: The persistent ProfileSwitcherBar at the top shows the pill 'CHILD MODE' (blue) on the entire parent-management flow: Parent Settings, Manage Tutors, Invite a Tutor, and the Rescind dialog. This is the exact inversion the audit was told to check for — a parent-only surface displayed under a child-mode badge. Root cause (app_shell.dart ProfileSwitcherBar, ~line 437-444): the badge is derived from activeProfile.profileMode, and entering parent mode via the PIN gate elevates authorization WITHOUT switching the active profile away from the child. So a parent invoking/revoking tutors is told they are in CHILD MODE. Misleading at best; at worst it undermines the mental model that tutor management is a parental control. The badge should reflect the parent-elevated context (or be suppressed) on these PIN-guarded surfaces.

findings.title: Empty Manage Tutors shows no 'No tutors invited.' hint — bare 'Invite a tutor' button only
findings.permutation: data=empty, font 1.0 and 1.3; reproduced on first entry, after rescind, and re-entry
findings.detail: manage_tutors_screen.dart lines 168-179 render localized 'No tutors invited.' (manageTutorsNoTutors) when the grants list resolves empty. Across every empty-state capture and uiautomator dump, that text node is ABSENT from the UI tree; there is also no LinearProgressIndicator/ProgressBar node and no error text. The screen shows only the child name header and the 'Invite a tutor' button with no status copy. Net user impact: an owner with zero tutors gets no confirmation the list is empty (vs. still loading/failed). The grants provider (outgoingTutorGrantsProvider, a network-only listTutorGrants Cloud Function FutureProvider) never logs an Async state via the riverpod observer, suggesting it may sit unresolved while the loading indicator (a zero-visibility LinearProgressIndicator) renders nothing — either way the empty-state affordance is effectively missing.

findings.title: Inconsistent section-label casing: 'ACTIVE (n)' all-caps vs 'Pending (n)' title-case
findings.permutation: data with grants; verified pending label rendered, active label from l10n
findings.detail: manageTutorsActiveSection => 'ACTIVE ($count)' (uppercase) while manageTutorsPendingSection => 'Pending ($count)' (title case). On a screen that can show both section dividers stacked for one child, the two headers render in different casing styles — a visual-consistency defect. They should share one casing convention.

findings.title: Edit Learner: Child/Adult toggle is interactive but the selected mode is silently discarded on Save
findings.permutation: adult mode, font 1.0, Edit dialog on LoopA (adult row)
findings.detail: In the Edit Learner dialog the Child/Adult SegmentedButton responds to taps and visually toggles (verified: switched LoopA from Adult to Child, checkmark moved). On Save the row still reads 'Adult mode' - the mode change has no effect. Root cause: editProfileFlow() in learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/profile_edit_delete_actions.dart calls repo.updateProfile(id, displayName, avatarIndex) and never passes the selected mode (the StatefulWidget tracks _mode and lets the user change it, but it is dropped). The code comment at lines 130-131 says 'Mode is shown but not editable' yet the control is NOT disabled. This is a control-that-does-nothing UX bug and a safety concern: a parent could believe they demoted an adult profile to child (which gates adult-only surfaces behind a PIN) when nothing changed. Same dialog: the avatar IS persisted while mode is not, with zero visual cue distinguishing the live control from the dead one.

findings.title: Deleted child profile reappears after an app restart (offline-first resurrection)
findings.permutation: adult mode, delete TestChildZ then cold-relaunch
findings.detail: Created child 'TestChildZ' (with PIN), deleted it via the row menu -> the list correctly dropped to 3 rows and the delete held across in-session navigation away/back. After the app was relaunched (cold start), TestChildZ reappeared both on the 'Who is learning?' profile selector and in Manage Learners. deleteProfileFlow is offline-first (deletes locally then enqueues the cloud delete to the outbox); on cold restart a cloud re-pull appears to resurrect the profile before the outbox delete propagates. From the user's view: 'I deleted this child, restarted, and it came back.' This is a data-integrity / trust issue. (Caveat: could be eventual-consistency that self-heals after a full sync, but it is observable and surprising at restart.)

findings.title: At font_scale 1.3 the Edit Learner dialog hides the entire avatar picker behind the keyboard on open
findings.permutation: font_scale 1.3, Edit dialog (autofocus keyboard up)
findings.detail: The Edit Learner dialog autofocuses the name field, so the soft keyboard is up by default. At 1.3 font scale the enlarged dialog content plus the keyboard pushes the 'Choose Avatar' section and its fixed-height (SizedBox height:60) avatar row completely below the fold, and the Child/Adult toggle row is clipped mid-button. The avatar picker is unreachable until the user manually dismisses the keyboard. At rest (keyboard down) the dialog renders fine. Affects accessibility-font users trying to change an avatar.

findings.title: Add-learner FAB has no accessibility label (empty content-desc)
findings.permutation: adult mode, baseline list
findings.detail: The primary 'add learner' action (FAB) exposes no accessible name to TalkBack/screen readers; it announces only as an unlabeled button. The per-row avatar tap targets in the Edit dialog likewise have empty content-desc (no 'Avatar 1, star' style labels). Add a tooltip/Semantics label (e.g. l10n.addProfile) to the FAB.

findings.title: Add vs Edit use two inconsistent mode-selection UIs and there is no name-length limit
findings.permutation: adult mode, Add dialog vs Edit dialog, long-name input
findings.detail: The Add Profile dialog presents mode as two big descriptive cards, while the Edit dialog presents it as a compact segmented pill - inconsistent patterns for the same concept (and in Edit the control is non-functional, see P1). Separately, name input accepts arbitrarily long values with no max-length: a 64-char name is created and the list row wraps across 3 lines with arbitrary mid-token breaks (no ellipsis, no overflow stripe, so not a crash - cosmetic). Consider a sane max length and unifying the two dialogs.

findings.title: ManageGrants screen and its empty-state are UNREACHABLE when the tutor has zero grants (dead UI / no entry path)
findings.permutation: Tutor test-loop-a@orvex.test, data state = empty (0 grants)
findings.detail: Signed in as the tutor and reached 'Who is learning?' — the account has zero own profiles and zero incoming grants, so the 'Talmid Profiles' section (which hosts the View-invitations and Manage-tutoring-grants rows) does not render at all. The ManageGrants route /tutor/my-grants is only ever pushed from those two grant-conditional rows; there is no deep-link, notification, or menu entry. Consequently ManageGrantsScreen's _EmptyGrantsView ('No tutoring relationships' / 'When a parent invites you to tutor their child, the grant will appear here.') is effectively dead code: the only state in which it would render (grants.isEmpty) is the exact state in which no UI path exists to open the screen. A tutor can never see this empty state. This is also why the screen could not be audited live.

findings.title: Tutor account-switcher 'Profiles' section is empty for a profile-less tutor (only 'Add Profile' under the header)
findings.permutation: Tutor test-loop-a@orvex.test, profile-less (DEC-6/DEC-21 path)
findings.detail: The bottom-sheet switcher shows a 'Profiles' header with NO profile rows beneath it — just the 'Add Profile' and 'Skip to Settings' actions. A header with zero items below it reads as a missing/broken list rather than an intentional empty state. For a profile-less tutor the 'Profiles' header should be suppressed or paired with an explicit empty hint.

findings.title: manageGrantsResign confirmation dialog body interpolates childProfileId (raw Firestore id) as the child name in the resignation notification path
findings.permutation: Active grant resign flow (static, screen unreachable at runtime)
findings.detail: The on-screen resign dialog correctly uses childDisplayLabel ('Talmid' fallback, never the raw id). But the fire-and-forget parent notification passes grant.childProfileId (the raw Firestore profile id) as childName. The same screen takes care never to surface the raw id to the user (per the M3 comments) yet ships it into the parent-facing resignation notification, where it can render as a NONSENSE internal id instead of a human name. Could not confirm the rendered notification because the screen is unreachable, but the code path is unambiguous.

findings.title: Pending-invite rows on ManageGrants have no accept/decline affordance (read-only), contrary to the audited control set
findings.permutation: Pending grant section (static)
findings.detail: The task's expected controls (accept/decline, enter tutored session) are NOT on this screen. ManageGrants renders pending grants as inert, status-only rows (a 'Pending' chip, no button). Accept/decline is handled elsewhere (the View-invitations row routes here, but here there is no way to act on a pending invite). A tutor who opens this screen via the 'Manage tutoring grants' row while a pending invite exists sees a Pending row they cannot act on — a likely dead-end. 'Enter tutored session' is on the profile-picker _TutoredChildRow, not here. Flagging the divergence so the expected control coverage is recorded as a gap rather than silently 'present'.

findings.title: Rapid double-tap on Send pops TWO screens — user lands on Parent Settings, not Manage Tutors
findings.permutation: rapid double-tap on Send (no-settle)
findings.detail: Typed a valid email and tapped Send twice with no settle. The invite was sent correctly (exactly ONE invite created — data is fine), but the app navigated back TWO levels and landed on Parent Settings instead of Manage Tutors. Root cause in invite_tutor_screen.dart: on success _sendInvite calls `await Navigator.of(context).maybePop()` (line 112). The Send FilledButton is only guarded by `_isLoading || !_emailValid` (line 223); there is no debounce, so a second tap fired during the navigation transition reaches the now-revealed Manage Tutors screen and triggers an extra pop. Net effect: a fast double-tap disorients the user (they end up a screen too far back and never see the new pending invite they just created).

findings.title: No confirmation dialog before sending an invite that grants a stranger access to the child's learning profile
findings.permutation: valid email — send
findings.detail: The orchestration brief listed a 'confirm dialog' as a control to exercise, but none exists. Tapping 'Send invite' fires the invite immediately (invite_tutor_screen.dart _sendInvite calls the use case directly with no AlertDialog). Given the body copy explicitly says the tutor will 'accept access to this child's learning profile' — a privacy-/access-granting action — the absence of any confirmation step (and the lack of an in-field warning about typos in the destination email) is a UX/safety gap for a parental-control surface. The success snackbar is also identical for a fresh invite vs a re-send of an already-pending email, giving no signal which occurred.

findings.title: Re-sending an invite to an already-pending email shows the same 'Invite sent!' success with no 'already invited' feedback
findings.permutation: duplicate-email re-send
findings.detail: Typed the exact email that already had a Pending invite. The form did not warn, the Send button enabled, and on send the snackbar reported success identically to a first-time invite. The backend correctly de-duplicated (the Pending count stayed at 1, so no double row / no stale count — good), but the UI gave no indication this was a duplicate/re-send. A parent cannot tell whether a second email was actually dispatched or silently merged.

findings.title: Email field has no accessibility label (uiautomator NAF=true, empty content-desc)
findings.permutation: empty/initial state; also at font 1.3
findings.detail: The TextFormField declares a Material `labelText` (invite_tutor_screen.dart line 179) but the rendered edit node exposes no content-description and is flagged Not-Accessibility-Friendly by uiautomator. A TalkBack user focusing the field would hear no purpose label. The visible label/hint render fine; this is a screen-reader-only gap on the single most important input on the screen.

findings.title: Header still shows 'CHILD MODE' badge (LoopChild) throughout the parent-only Invite a Tutor flow
findings.permutation: all states
findings.detail: Every screenshot of this parent-only flow (Manage Tutors and Invite a Tutor) keeps the global 'CHILD MODE' badge and the LoopChild avatar in the header, even though Parent Settings was entered and these are admin-only surfaces. The mode chrome contradicts the context (a parent-only surface under a child-mode badge — matches the rubric's 'wrong mode for the context' check). It is the shared app header rather than this screen's own widget, but it is misleading on this screen.

findings.title: Validation is present-but-lenient: accepts malformed addresses like 'a@b.c' / 'foo@.com'; no proactive inline error
findings.permutation: junk (notanemail), partial (foo@bar), trailing whitespace
findings.detail: Validation correctly disables Send for clearly-junk input ('notanemail', 'foo@bar') — good. But `_emailValid` is only `text.trim().contains('@') && contains('.')`, so structurally invalid addresses (e.g. 'a@.b', 'foo@.com', '@x.y') would pass and enable Send. Because the button is disabled while invalid, the `inviteTutorInvalidEmail` error branch (lines 62-66) and the `errorText` are effectively unreachable from the UI — there is never a proactive inline validation message, only button gating. Trailing whitespace is benign: a TrimLeadingSpaceFormatter plus `.trim()` (lines 55/60/175) clean it before send, so the 'aaa@orvex.test ' case I saw enable Send is trimmed correctly.

findings.title: AcceptInvite screen unreachable — no pending tutor grant for the signed-in account, and the documented /invite deep link is not registered in AndroidManifest
findings.permutation: data-state=no-pending-invite; account LoopA / UID WrUGgVgkhfRS5wdQJI5b0fb3Zjt2
findings.detail: The AcceptInvite screen (lib/features/tutoring/presentation/screens/accept_invite_screen.dart) has only two in-app entry points: a pending-invite row in the profile-picker (_buildPendingInvites, line 164) and the Settings 'Talmid profiles' tile (_PendingInvitesSection, settings_screen.dart:685). Both render ONLY when ref.watch(pendingTutorInvitesProvider)/incomingTutorGrantsProvider returns a Firestore grant whose tutorEmail == the signed-in account and state==pending. The current account (UID WrUGgVgkhfRS5wdQJI5b0fb3Zjt2, read from shared_prefs flutter.last_active_account_id) has NO such grant: Manage Learners shows only own profiles, and the Settings 'Talmid profiles' section is entirely absent (it short-circuits to SizedBox.shrink when both grant lists are empty). Constructing a pending grant needs a SECOND parent account to invite this account's email (or direct Firestore seeding) — server state a read-only auditor cannot create. SEPARATELY, the screen's own doc comment (lines 10-11) and the router (app_router.dart:316, AutoRoute path '/invite') advertise '/invite?token=<grantId>' as the deep-link entry, but AndroidManifest.xml registers an intent-filter ONLY for pathPrefix '/sign-in' (lines 42-50) — there is NO filter for '/invite'. The intent attempt returned 'Activity not started, unable to resolve Intent ... act=VIEW dat=https://torah-study-tracker.firebaseapp.com/invite'. So the documented external deep-link entry point is non-functional: a real invite email linking to /invite would fail to open this screen from outside the app. This is a latent product defect (broken advertised entry) and is also why this audit pass is blocked.

findings.title: Search-field hint scrambles in bidi: 'Search <Hebrew>…' renders with the ellipsis detached and floated to the far-left edge
findings.permutation: empty-query state, hebrew-terms ON (curriculum label = Hebrew 'תלמוד בבלי'), font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: The hint template is searchFieldHint = 'Search $label…' (app_localizations_en.dart:2418-2420). When the curriculum label is Hebrew (RTL) — as it is whenever Hebrew Terms is ON — the LTR 'Search' word, the RTL Hebrew run, and the neutral trailing '…' get reordered by the Unicode bidi algorithm. On screen the hint reads (left-to-right) '…תלמוד בבלי Search': the ellipsis is pulled to the far LEFT edge and 'Search' is pushed to the far RIGHT, so the intended 'Search [name]…' phrase is visually fragmented. The TextField uses no Directionality/bidi-isolate around the injected label, so the mixed-direction hint is unstable. Cosmetic but visible on the default (Hebrew-terms ON) configuration of the very first state a user sees on this screen.

findings.title: No-results / search-field echo of the query is a single unbounded line — fits edge-to-edge on tablet but will clip/wrap unbounded on phone widths
findings.permutation: very-long query (90+ chars and 47-char tokens), no-results state, font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: noResultsForQuery(query) echoes the raw query verbatim inside quotes with textAlign.center and no maxLines/overflow handling (content_search_screen.dart:137). On this 2560px tablet a 90-character token rendered as one centered line that touched both edges (closing quote nearly off the right edge) without hard-clipping, and the 47-char case at font 1.3 also just fit. There is no clamp, so on a narrower phone the same input either wraps to many lines or (in the TextField above) scrolls; the echoed message has no truncation safeguard. Robustness gap rather than a confirmed visible break on this device — flagged because the worst case was borderline at tablet width.

findings.title: No clear (X) affordance in the search field — query can only be erased with the keyboard backspace
findings.permutation: results state and no-results state, all nusach/font permutations
findings.detail: The AppBar TextField uses border: InputBorder.none and defines no suffixIcon/clear button (content_search_screen.dart:95-110). The 'clear' control named in the audit brief does not exist as an on-screen affordance: the only way to clear a typed query is keyboard backspace (or Back to leave). On a touch device with a long query this is a friction point and means there is no one-tap reset to the empty 'Enter a search term above' state. Functional clear-via-backspace works correctly; this is a missing-affordance observation.

findings.title: Hebrew-terms breadcrumb is laid out left-to-right (LTR) with right-pointing chevrons, inverting the hierarchy for an RTL reader
findings.permutation: Mishna daily-task × Sephardi × Hebrew-terms ON × With-nikud × font 1.0 (also reproduced in Chumash browse breadcrumb)
findings.detail: When Hebrew Terms is ON the TextDisplay breadcrumb renders the domain terms in Hebrew script ('זרעים › ברכות › פרק א › משנה ב') but keeps the English LTR layout: the broadest term (זרעים / Seder) sits on the LEFT and the most-specific (משנה ב / Mishna) on the RIGHT, with '›' chevrons pointing right. For a native Hebrew reader scanning right-to-left this reverses the hierarchy — the eye hits the most-specific node first. The same direction issue is present on the Browse 'Browse Content' breadcrumb (חומש › בראשית). The individual Hebrew words and gematriya render correctly; only the breadcrumb container/separator direction was not flipped to RTL. A pure text-only loop sees the correct Hebrew strings and would mark this 'present and correct' — the directional defect is only visible with eyes.

findings.title: Hebrew breadcrumb orphans the gematriya letter onto its own wrapped line ('משנה' / 'ב')
findings.permutation: Mishna daily-task × Hebrew-terms ON × font 1.0 and font 1.3
findings.detail: In Hebrew-terms mode the breadcrumb 'זרעים › ברכות › פרק א › משנה ב' wraps so that the gematriya value 'ב' falls alone on the second line, separated from its label 'משנה'. The number is visually detached from the term it qualifies. Minor but reads awkwardly; a non-breaking grouping of 'משנה ב' would avoid the orphan.

findings.title: Prev-chevron affordance for the same Mishna is inconsistent depending on how the screen was reached (browse vs. post-completion)
findings.permutation: Mishna 2 reached via next-chevron from Mishna 1 (prev ENABLED) vs. Mishna 2 reached via Mark-complete auto-advance (prev DISABLED)
findings.detail: Identical content (Berakhos Perek 1 Mishna 2) shows the previous-item chevron ENABLED when you browse into it from Mishna 1, but DISABLED after you Mark-complete Mishna 1 (which shifts the daily-task navigation boundary). I tapped the grayed chevron and it did nothing, confirming a genuine disabled state. Practical consequence: immediately after completing a mishna the learner can no longer page BACK to re-read the text they just finished via the chevron — the just-completed item is dropped from the navigation set. The two navigation contexts (full-curriculum browse vs. remaining-daily-tasks) are conflated under the same chevron UI, producing a confusing/inconsistent affordance.

findings.title: TextDisplay exposes NO in-screen nikud toggle, script toggle, or share control
findings.permutation: All TextDisplay states (Mishna daily-task and Chumash browse-leaf)
findings.detail: The audit brief lists 'nikud/script toggles' and 'share' as controls to exercise on this screen. They do not exist here. The TextDisplay app bar contains only: Back (←) and prev/next chevrons (‹ ›). Nikud, nusach (Ashkenazi/Sephardi), and Hebrew-terms are all controlled GLOBALLY from Settings — there is no per-text quick toggle and no Share affordance anywhere on the reading screen. To change nikud while reading, the user must leave to Settings → toggle → navigate back. Whether intended or a gap, it means three of the five named controls for this screen are absent; recording so the orchestrator does not assume they were verified.

findings.title: Mishna view shows English 'Mark complete' / 'Next daily task' / 'Hebrew Text' / 'English Translation' labels even with Hebrew Terms ON
findings.permutation: Mishna daily-task × Hebrew-terms ON
findings.detail: With Hebrew Terms ON the curriculum nodes (seder/masechta/perek/mishna) correctly flip to Hebrew script + gematriya, but the section badges ('Hebrew Text', 'English Translation') and the action buttons ('Mark complete', 'Next daily task') stay English. This is arguably acceptable since they are UI chrome rather than domain curriculum terms (and the known MaterialApp locale bug keeps chrome English) — flagged as a consistency observation, not a hard defect. The toggle itself works correctly for the domain terms it governs.

findings.title: Content-type divergence: Chumash/Tanach browse-leaf has no translation pane and no completion/Mark-complete controls, unlike the Mishna view
findings.permutation: Chumash browse-leaf (Bereishit Perek Alef) vs. Mishna daily-task
findings.detail: Both surfaces are 'TextDisplay' but render very differently. The Mishna (daily-task) view has a Hebrew card + an 'English Translation' card + 'Mark complete' / 'Next daily task' buttons. The Chumash browse-leaf is a continuous-scroll chapter (verses numbered in gematriya א/ב/ג…) with NO English translation pane and NO completion/next buttons — only the chevron pager. Maqaf (־) and nikud render cleanly. Not necessarily a bug (browse is read-only, daily-task is trackable), but the absence of any translation for Chumash and the absence of a 'mark as learned' path from browse are worth confirming against intent.

findings.title: Greeting says 'Good morning' at 12:49 PM (time-of-day mismatch) — observed on Dashboard during navigation, outside target screen
findings.permutation: LoopChild Dashboard at 12:49 (in-passing observation, not the TextDisplay target)
findings.detail: While re-entering the LoopChild profile to restore settings, the Dashboard header read 'Good morning' at 12:49 PM. This is on the Dashboard, not TextDisplay, so it is out of my screen scope and offered only as a drive-by note for whoever audits the Dashboard. No action expected from this TextDisplay pass.

findings.title: Header labels lifetime LEARN events as "chazaros" (reviews); header contradicts the leaf rows which all show "Live" with zero chazaros
findings.permutation: data=populated, hebrew-terms ON and OFF
findings.detail: The header subtitle reads "7 total chazaros" but the user has done ZERO reviews — each leaf has only the initial limud, so every leaf renders "Live" with no chazara count. In code lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart:471 sets totalChazaros = completions.length, counting EVERY completion row (limud + chazara) per its own doc comment ('Every event (limud or chazara) increments the counter'), then renders it through domainTermLabels.totalChazaros() whose string is literally '{count} total chazaros'. So initial-learn events are mislabeled as reviews. The same screen visibly self-contradicts: header claims 7 chazaros while every leaf says it was only learned (Live, no chazaros). A user with N learned-but-never-reviewed items always sees a non-zero 'total chazaros' that is actually their learn count.

findings.title: Pluralization broken for count=1 on the Lifetime header and tier counters ("1 items learned", "1 total chazaros", "1 Siyumim earned")
findings.permutation: data state where a counter == 1 (currently 7, so not visually triggered; code-certain)
findings.detail: None of these ARB strings use ICU {count, plural,...}; they hard-concatenate the noun in plural form. At count=1 the header card (lifetime_knowledge_screen.dart:225/233) renders "1 items learned" and "1 total chazaros" (should be "1 item learned" / "1 total chazara"); the Lifetime tile accessibility/semantic label becomes "1 items in lifetime"; the Siyumim tier counter becomes "1 Siyumim earned" (already wrong even at >1 because the term is the plural). This is exactly the '1 Items' pluralization defect class. Not reproducible visually on LoopA because counts are 7/0, but unconditional in code for any value of 1.

findings.title: Mixed nusach on one screen: curriculum/book names honor Sephardi (Bereshit, Shemot) but the domain term "chazaros" is hard-coded Ashkenazi (-os)
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms=OFF, nusach=Sephardi
findings.detail: With Pronunciation set to Sephardi, the breakdown correctly transliterates book names with -ot/-it endings, but the header card still says "chazaros" (Ashkenazi). domain_term_labels.dart:239 `String get chazaros => _useHebrew ? 'חזרות' : 'Chazaros';` takes no nusach variant — unlike shabbos()/havdalah() which DO accept a TransliterationVariant. In Sephardi it should read "chazarot". Same hard-Ashkenazi issue applies to siyumim/mishnayos-style terms. Result: two transliteration conventions visible on a single screen.

findings.title: Hebrew-terms ON yields a mixed-script screen: stat-card headline is Hebrew while all UI chrome (title, toggle, CTA) and per-leaf provenance stay English
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms=ON
findings.detail: The Hebrew-terms toggle swaps only domain-term strings (itemsLearnedCount/totalChazaros and curriculum names) to Hebrew script, leaving the surrounding chrome and the provenance word "Live" in English. The single-line headline "פריטים נלמדו 7" also places an Arabic numeral 7 at the visual left of an RTL Hebrew phrase. Per the known MaterialApp locale:null limitation the chrome cannot localize, but the half-Hebrew/half-English result is visually jarring and the "Live" Latin word sits inside otherwise all-Hebrew rows. Numeral is Arabic, not gematriya, in Hebrew-script mode.

findings.title: "Add items I learned previously" CTA did not navigate on repeated taps
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms=OFF/ON, populated
findings.detail: The footer CTA card is wired to push LifetimeMarkingRoute (lifetime_knowledge_screen.dart:169-171 InkWell onTap). Across five taps at distinct points inside the visibly-rendered card no navigation occurred. Caveat: the card's lower edge sits very close to the system gesture-nav strip, so taps near the bottom could be consumed by the OS inset rather than a true dead target — this needs confirmation with a hardware/devtools tap. Reporting as a possible non-functional CTA pending that confirmation. (By contrast, the curriculum-card expand InkWell directly above responded reliably, so taps do register on this screen.)

findings.title: Header exposes internal "level N" id to the user (and the number is a wrong value)
findings.permutation: All — Hebrew-terms ON/OFF, Ashkenazi & Sephardi, font 1.0 & 1.3
findings.detail: The "Mark as lifetime learned" box renders the raw string "Selected: {count} • level {level}" verbatim to the user, e.g. "Selected: 0 • level 1". This is exactly the internal "level N" id the screen is supposed to NOT show in the header. Worse, the number is computed wrong: at the top level it shows "level 1", but after drilling ONE level into Seder Moed (depth 2) the header reads "level 6" (lm_07/lm_22), and inside Bereshit it reads "level 5" (lm_27). The value equals the COUNT of items in the current list (6 masechtos in Moed, 5 perakim shown), not the hierarchy depth. So the user sees a nonsense "level" number that changes per folder size. Source: lifetimeMarkAsLearnedLine = "Selected: {count} • level {level}" fed by the buggy _currentLevel getter which returns _currentDisplayItems.length. The 'level' token should be removed from the user-facing header entirely.

findings.title: Persisted (already-learned) rows are visually identical to freshly-selected rows; selection lingers after Save and after Clear
findings.permutation: After a save round-trip; both nuschaos; Hebrew-terms ON/OFF
findings.detail: After saving Seder Zeraim, the row shows a green filled checkbox + green highlight (MarkingRowVisual.direct, persisted branch). A brand-new manual selection (e.g. Seder Moed) renders with the EXACT same green checkbox/highlight (lm_23_resume). There is no visual distinction between "already learned/persisted" and "currently selected this session" — the user cannot tell what they are about to commit vs what is already committed. Compounding it: pressing "Clear selection" sets the header to "Selected: 0" and disables Save, yet the persisted Zeraim row STAYS green and checked (lm_11_zeraim_zoom) — looks like Clear failed. And after a successful Save the selection is NOT cleared (lm_10/lm_24: row stays green, header still "Selected: 1"), so a user can re-tap Save with no feedback that nothing new will happen.

findings.title: Save confirmation toast uses lazy "selection(s)" instead of singular for count = 1
findings.permutation: count = 1 save; reproduced with double-tap guard
findings.detail: Saving exactly one selection shows the toast "Marked 1 lifetime selection(s)." — the parenthetical "(s)" is the non-pluralized fallback flagged by the rubric for count=1. It should read "Marked 1 lifetime selection." (singular). The ARB key lifetimeMarkSavedCount = "Marked {count} lifetime selection(s)." has no ICU plural form, so every count (1 or many) shows "(s)".

findings.title: Hardware Back mid-flow silently discards a pending bulk selection with no confirmation
findings.permutation: Sephardi, Hebrew-terms OFF, font 1.0 (behavior is lever-independent)
findings.detail: With Seder Nashim selected but not yet saved, pressing the Android Back button navigated straight from the marking screen back to the curriculum list, discarding the pending selection with no 'discard unsaved changes?' prompt. For a bulk-marking flow where a user may have checked many items (or used Select-all), an accidental Back loses all of it silently. Low severity (standard navigation behavior) but worth a guard for large pending selections.

findings.title: "Select all in this list" button never toggles to a Deselect-all affordance even when everything is selected
findings.permutation: Mishnayos level 1, all 6 sedarim selected
findings.detail: After tapping 'Select all in this list', all 6 rows are checked (header 'Selected: 6'), but the button label stays 'Select all in this list' — tapping it again just re-selects the same set (no-op). A 'deselectAllInThisList' string already exists in app_en.arb (line 402) but is not wired up on this screen, so there is no one-tap way to clear just the current list; the only clear is the global 'Clear selection'. Minor usability gap.

findings.title: No Forgot Password / password-recovery affordance anywhere on the sign-in screen
findings.permutation: all states (font 1.0 & 1.3, online cloud mode)
findings.detail: The sign-in screen offers email + Secret Key, Sign In, Sign in with Google, Keep me signed in, and a single 'New to the Quest? Register Here' link — but NO 'Forgot password' link. Confirmed in code: lib/features/account/presentation/widgets/sign_in_actions.dart and sign_in_form.dart contain no reset/recovery affordance, and the only l10n forgot-password string is absent. A cloud (password) user who forgets their password has no recovery path from this screen. The task explicitly lists forgot-password as a required control; it does not exist.

findings.title: Error snackbar rendered in neutral slate-grey instead of an error/red color
findings.permutation: valid email + wrong password (online cloud sign-in)
findings.detail: On a wrong-password submit the snackbar reads 'Incorrect password. Please try again.' but is rendered on a muted slate-grey-blue background, so an authentication ERROR visually reads as a neutral/info toast. Root cause: _showError() in sign_in_screen.dart sets backgroundColor: AppTheme.brandCoralDeep, but brandCoralDeep is defined as Color(0xFF4E5E70) (a slate grey, not coral/red) in lib/core/theme/app_theme.dart:31. The constant is mis-named AND the error lacks any error-color affordance.

findings.title: Validation errors persist on fully-corrected fields until the next submit
findings.permutation: empty submit, then type valid email + password
findings.detail: After an empty-field submit shows 'Email is required' and 'Password is required', typing valid values into both fields does NOT clear the errors — the red borders and 'required' messages linger while the field content is clearly valid (e.g. email 'test-loop-c@orvex.test' with a non-empty password). The Form in sign_in_form.dart sets no autovalidateMode, so validation only re-runs on the next Sign In tap. Lingering/stale validation state per the rubric; AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction would clear errors as the user corrects them.

findings.title: Stale 'CloudUser ADULT MODE' profile/mode banner overlays the unauthenticated sign-in screen
findings.permutation: sign-in reached via add-account / post sign-out
findings.detail: The persistent top role-switcher banner shows 'CloudUser  ADULT MODE' (with the C avatar and the up/down switch chevron) sitting on top of the sign-in screen's own 'Welcome Back!' card. The same banner also persists on the post-sign-out Account Picker where the cloud account is flagged 'SIGN IN AGAIN'. A signed-in profile/mode identity is being shown on an auth surface that is supposed to be unauthenticated — a wrong-context/leftover-state surface (a different account's mode chrome above a fresh login form).

findings.title: Focused email field clips its value mid-character at font 1.3
findings.permutation: font_scale 1.3, email field focused with a long value
findings.detail: At font 1.3 with the field focused, 'test-loop-c@orvex.test' is cut at the right edge so it renders as 'test-loop-c@orvex.tes' + a clipped partial 't' ('tes1'-looking). It is the standard TextField horizontal-scroll-to-cursor behavior (the unfocused field at font 1.0 shows the full value, see /tmp/audit/signin_clean.png), so it is borderline-expected rather than a hard layout bug, but at large text the truncation reads as a broken/clipped value with no ellipsis.

findings.title: Offline data-loss warnings + all error snackbars render in slate-grey, not coral/red — a warning that doesn't read as a warning
findings.permutation: offline + font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: The two offline 'no cloud backup / your data stays only on this device' destructive-warning cards, their icons, and the offline-ack-required snackbar ('Please acknowledge the offline account warning...') all render in a muted blue-grey. Root cause: the theme constants NAMED coral are actually slate-grey — app_theme.dart lines 29-31: brandCoral=0xFF708090 (CSS SlateGray), brandCoralSoft=0xFFD8DEE3, brandCoralDeep=0xFF4E5E70. _showError() sets backgroundColor: AppTheme.brandCoralDeep and _buildAccountModeCard uses brandCoralSoft/brandCoralDeep for the warning cards/icons. So EVERY error and destructive warning on signup (duplicate-email, invalid-email, weak-password, generic errors, the data-loss caveats) carries zero red/warning urgency. By contrast the AccountPicker's 'SIGN IN AGAIN' badge uses a genuine red, proving a real warning color exists in the app — the signup warnings look anomalously calm. For an offline-first signup whose entire value-prop hinges on the user understanding 'your data will NOT be backed up,' this is a meaningful semantics/contrast defect.

findings.title: RenderFlex overflow stripes ('BOTTOM OVERFLOWED BY 1.2 PIXELS') on profile-picker cards under large text (font 1.3)
findings.permutation: font 1.3 (large text), reached via add-account/signup flow
findings.detail: At font_scale 1.3 the 'Who is learning?' profile-picker cards (LoopA ADULT MODE and RedeemKid CHILD MODE) show Flutter's yellow-and-black RenderFlex overflow hazard stripes reading 'BOTTOM OVERFLOWED BY 1.2 PIXELS', and the 'Tap to continue' caption is clipped to 'Tap to'. This screen sits directly on the add-account -> signup navigation path. Confirmed font-scale-specific: resetting to 1.0 removes the stripes and shows full 'Tap to continue'. The card heights are not accessibility/large-text safe.

findings.title: Signup screen shows a logged-in account chip (LoopA / ADULT MODE) while creating a brand-new, different account
findings.permutation: all (online + offline)
findings.detail: SignupRoute is pushed onto the app-shell stack (from the AccountPicker '+1 Add another account' dashed button, which calls context.router.push(SignupRoute())). The shell's persistent app bar — showing the currently-active account 'LoopA' and an 'ADULT MODE' chip plus an account-switcher control — remains visible on top of the signup form. So while the user is creating a NEW account with a different identity, the chrome advertises a different existing account and an interactive switcher. Wrong account/profile context for a create-account surface (rubric: 'Wrong account/profile/mode for the context').

findings.title: Task-specified 'confirm password' field and 'terms' control do not exist on this screen
findings.permutation: all
findings.detail: The audit brief lists 'confirm password' and 'terms' as controls to exercise, but the implementation has neither. There is exactly one password field (no confirm/mismatch path to test) and no terms-of-service / privacy acceptance checkbox. The only checkbox is the offline-acknowledge box, which appears solely in offline mode. If a confirm-password or terms gate is a product requirement, it is missing; if not, the spec/control list is stale. Either way 'password mismatch' cannot occur because there is no second field.

findings.title: Display-name validator allows trailing-space-only / unbounded names; no length cap and trimmed-empty not re-checked
findings.permutation: online, validation
findings.detail: validateDisplayName returns null for any non-empty raw string, but submit uses displayName.trim(). The TrimLeadingSpaceFormatter only strips LEADING spaces, so a value like 'a ' (trailing space) passes; and there is no maximum length. A 60-character name was accepted and rendered (horizontal-scrolls in the field with no overflow — graceful, but no guardrail). Edge cases of trimmed-empty or absurdly long display names are not defended at the validation layer. Low user-facing impact but a real input-validation gap.

findings.title: Inconsistent terminology/voice between Sign In and Signup screens for identical fields/concepts
findings.permutation: online (cross-screen)
findings.detail: Sign In labels the same inputs 'Your Email' / 'Secret Key' with playful copy ('Welcome Back!', 'New to the Quest? Register Here'), while Signup uses plain 'Email Address' / 'Create Password' ('Already exploring? Log In'). The cloud card wording also differs: Sign In says data is 'backed up and syncs across devices' whereas Signup says 'backed up and can sync across devices.' Same product concept, two voices — inconsistent and slightly confusing across the auth pair.

findings.title: Validation errors are stale until next submit (no onUserInteraction re-validation)
findings.permutation: online, validation
findings.detail: The Form has no autovalidateMode, so once an error is shown it persists even after the user has corrected the field — e.g. after typing a valid 'AuditName' the 'Display name is required' error stays until the next Sign Up tap. Minor UX friction; users may think a corrected field is still wrong.

findings.title: Tapping a SIGN-IN-AGAIN account enters it with NO re-authentication (auth gate bypassed)
findings.permutation: multiple accounts, SIGN IN AGAIN card (Loop Test C), font 1.0
findings.detail: The 'Loop Test C' card is explicitly labeled SIGN IN AGAIN with a red warning triangle, signalling the cached credential is invalid and re-auth is required. Tapping the card does NOT present any password/credential challenge — it switches straight into that account's profile picker ('Who is learning?') and the switch persists across an app relaunch. A card that promises re-authentication and instead grants entry with zero auth is a security/correctness defect: either the gate is missing or the badge is lying. The trailing red triangle is also inert (tapping it does nothing — /tmp/audit/ap_tap_triangle.png), so there is no dedicated re-auth affordance at all.

findings.title: Account list reorders non-deterministically between visits; active account is not pinned
findings.permutation: multiple accounts, repeated entry to picker, font 1.0
findings.detail: On first display the active account (Loop Test A, marked with a chevron) is at the top; on a later visit the SIGN-IN-AGAIN account (Loop Test C) floats to the top and the active account drops below it. The ordering is unstable across visits. This is dangerous combined with the rapid-tap/auth-bypass behavior: a user reaching for the same card position can land on a different account. The active account is not pinned/highlighted consistently.

findings.title: Rapid taps on 'Add another account' silently switch into a different account instead of opening Create Account
findings.permutation: adversarial rapid triple-tap on Add-account button, font 1.0
findings.detail: A no-settle triple-tap on the dashed '+1 Add another account (3 slots remaining)' button did not reliably open the CreateAccount screen; instead the app ended up in Loop Test C's profile picker and persisted that account selection. This is a debounce / race / re-layout-during-tap defect: taps intended for the add-account button are consumed by a reordered account card. Combined with the missing re-auth gate, rapid interaction can switch the active account without the user intending to.

findings.title: Back from the profile picker (reached via account switch) exits the app to the OS launcher instead of returning to the account picker
findings.permutation: Back mid-flow after selecting an account, font 1.0
findings.detail: After tapping an account and landing on 'Who is learning?', pressing the system Back button drops the user straight out of the app to the Android launcher rather than back to 'Choose an Account'. There is no back stack between the account picker and the profile picker in this entry path. A user who taps the wrong account (especially given the unstable ordering) cannot Back out to re-choose — they get ejected from the app and must relaunch.

findings.title: Create Account form is left-anchored as a narrow column on tablet, leaving 60%+ of the screen blank
findings.permutation: Add-account -> Create Account, tablet 2560x1600, font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: On the wide tablet the CreateAccount form (reached via the AccountPicker's Add-account button) renders as a narrow phone-width column pinned to the left edge instead of being centered/constrained-and-centered. The large empty right region looks broken on a tablet. The account picker cards themselves do span full width, so the inconsistency is jarring within the same flow.

findings.title: Sign Out and Delete Account icons render as blank solid-red discs with no glyph in the account bottom sheet
findings.permutation: Account bottom sheet (entry point to AccountPicker), font 1.0
findings.detail: In the ACCOUNT bottom sheet that gates the 'Switch account' entry to the picker, the two destructive actions (Sign Out, Delete Account) have icon containers filled solid red with no icon glyph inside, while every other row shows its glyph. Destructive actions losing their iconography is exactly where a clear visual cue matters most. Matches the rubric 'icon rendered as a blank disc with no glyph.'

findings.title: AccountPicker ignores system font scaling (1.3) while the sibling Create Account screen honors it — inconsistent accessibility
findings.permutation: font_scale 1.3 vs 1.0 on AccountPicker and CreateAccount
findings.detail: With system font_scale set to 1.3, the AccountPicker text does not enlarge at all (the app clamps/ignores textScaler on this screen), yet the CreateAccount screen reached one tap later DOES scale. Accessibility users who enlarge system text get no benefit on the account-selection screen, and the two screens behave inconsistently. No clipping or overflow was observed on either screen at 1.3 — this is an accessibility-compliance gap, not a layout break.

findings.title: Settings account header shows mismatched email after account interaction (TestParent profile shown with test-loop-a email while top bar had read Loop Test C)
findings.permutation: after tapping SIGN-IN-AGAIN account then selecting TestParent profile, font 1.0
findings.detail: The active-account identity is inconsistent across surfaces after switching: the top bar briefly read 'Loop Test C', the profile picker showed C's profiles, but Settings and the account sheet then report the email test-loop-a@orvex.test. Either the displayed email is stale or the account switch only partially took effect. Users cannot trust which account/data they are actually operating in — a real concern given the auth-bypass and reorder findings above.

findings.title: Hebrew-Terms = English setting is ignored across the entire curriculum/goal track wizard — every domain label renders in Hebrew script
findings.permutation: Hebrew-Terms=English, Adult Mode, font 1.0
findings.detail: On the profile-creation step I explicitly set the 'Hebrew Terms' toggle to English (confirmed in /tmp/audit/onb_22.png, left white pill). The code at onboarding_profile_creation_step.dart:104 persists this via useHebrewTermsProvider.set(false). Yet every subsequent track-wizard step renders ALL domain terms in Hebrew script only, with no English transliteration: curriculum picker (STEP 1) shows משניות / תלמוד בבלי / חומש / נ"ך / משנה ברורה / תנ"ך / תלמוד ירושלמי / משנה תורה / מוסר; programs show הלכה יומית / ערוך השולחן יומי; units show סימנים / סעיפים; review step header is 'How do you want to חזרה?'. curriculum_picker_step.dart:185 only shows the English subtitle `if (!terms.isHebrew)` — the absence of any English line on screen proves terms.isHebrew evaluated TRUE despite the English selection (provider appears reset when the offline signup invalidates userDatabaseProvider / switches DB). The domain oracle requires English-mode labels to NOT contain Hebrew-script chars (U+0590-05FF) unless intended; the user's explicit English choice is silently discarded for the whole curriculum/goal flow.

findings.title: 'Continue' button on the goal step (STEP 6) is blocked by an overlapping tap region of the 'Set Deadline' card — taps switch goal mode / open the date picker instead of advancing
findings.permutation: goal step STEP 6, target-pace mode, font 1.0
findings.detail: Repeatedly reproduced: tapping the visually-clear, enabled blue 'Continue' button at the bottom of STEP 6 does NOT advance the wizard. Instead it lands on the 'Set Deadline' card's hit region, flipping the goal type to Deadline and opening the 'Select Hebrew date' picker — even when the deadline card is visually dimmed in target-pace mode. The Continue button and the deadline card occupy colliding tap zones (tap targets colliding). This is a functional blocker: a user cannot reliably press Continue, and accidental taps silently change their goal configuration. ~10 attempts at varying y all hit the card; advancing required scrolling content up to separate the two, and even then most taps hit the card.

findings.title: 'Starts:' label on the Halacha-Yomis program card shows the program NAME where a start DATE belongs
findings.permutation: Join a Program step STEP 2, font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: The first program card reads (accessibility tree): 'הלכה יומית\nDaily halacha study following the Shulchan Aruch cycle.\nStarts: הלכה יומית'. The 'Starts:' field (calendar icon prefix, implying a date) is bound to the program name 'הלכה יומית' instead of an actual start date — a NONSENSE value (a name where a date belongs). The sibling card uses a different format ('DAILY CALENDAR'), so the two cards' metadata lines are also inconsistent.

findings.title: RenderFlex overflow ('OVERFLOWED BY 37 PIXELS') on the scope-step breadcrumb at font 1.3
findings.permutation: scope step STEP 3, font 1.3
findings.detail: At font_scale 1.3, the breadcrumb row on 'All of it, or just a section?' (STEP 3) — 'משנה ברורה ← ספר selection' — shows the classic yellow/black debug overflow stripe with 'RIGHT OVERFLOWED BY 37 PIXELS' on the right edge; the word 'selection' is clipped. A Row/breadcrumb is not constraining its children for large-text users. Visible only at 1.3; clean at 1.0.

findings.title: Estimated-finish gematriya year is wrong for far-future dates (renders a far-PAST Hebrew year)
findings.permutation: goal step STEP 6, target-pace = 1 se'if/week, Calendar=Hebrew
findings.detail: With pace floored at 1 se'if/week for the full Mishnah Berurah (≈17,397 items ≈ 334 years out, ~year 6120 / 2360 CE), the 'Estimated finish' shows 'כ׳ חשוון ק״כ'. The year 'ק״כ' = 120, which reads as Hebrew year 5120 (≈1360 CE) — a date ~666 years in the PAST. The thousands component (ו'=6000) is dropped, so any finish date beyond Hebrew year 6000 renders as a nonsensical past date. At pace 14 the date 'תת״י' (=810→5810) happens to look plausible, masking the bug; it surfaces at low pace / long horizon.

findings.title: Pluralization bug: '1 DAYS' (custom cycle ring) and '1 study days' (deadline estimate) for count = 1
findings.permutation: review step STEP 5 + goal step STEP 6, font 1.0
findings.detail: Two count=1 pluralization defects. (1) Custom Cycle ring on STEP 5 shows '1 DAYS' (a11y: '1\nDAYS') — should be '1 DAY'; the adjacent '7 DAYS' is correct. (2) The deadline-mode estimate on STEP 6 reads 'About 17397 סעיפים per study day, across 1 study days to finish the scope by the deadline' — 'across 1 study days' should be '1 study day'. Matches the rubric's '1 study days' example exactly.

findings.title: Degenerate default: deadline pre-set to TODAY yields impossible '17397 items in 1 study day' plan, shown as the default estimate
findings.permutation: goal step STEP 6, deadline mode (default), font 1.0
findings.detail: Switching to 'Set Deadline' defaults the date to today (כ"ו סיוון תשפ"ו = Jun 11 2026, the current date). The app then computes 'About 17397 סעיפים per study day, across 1 study days ... (≈17397 items)' — i.e. it asks the user to complete all 17,397 se'ifim in a single day. A deadline-of-today default produces a meaningless plan with no warning or floor.

findings.title: Mixed Hebrew/English in single phrases on the goal step ('סעיפים Per week', 'סימנים | סעיפים' vs 'Per day | Per week')
findings.permutation: goal step STEP 6, Hebrew-Terms=English, font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: The Target Pace card header literally reads 'סעיפים Per week' (Hebrew noun + English period in one line). The unit segmented control shows Hebrew 'סימנים' / 'סעיפים' while the adjacent period control is English 'Per day' / 'Per week'. In an English-terms profile these item-unit labels should be transliterated ('Simanim' / 'Se'ifim'). Half-translated phrase within one control group.

findings.title: Study-days list mixes scripts: six days in English, Saturday alone as Hebrew 'שבת'
findings.permutation: study days step STEP 4, Hebrew-Terms=English, font 1.0
findings.detail: On 'Study Days', Sunday–Friday render in English (Latin), but the 7th row renders as Hebrew 'שבת' with avatar 'ש' (a11y: 'ש\nשבת'). In an English-terms profile this is an inconsistent half-translated row — either all days transliterated or all Hebrew, not six-and-one. (Also: שבת/Shabbos defaults to ON as a study day, which is a questionable default for this domain, but the concrete bug is the mixed script.)

findings.title: Curriculum scope item shows '697 סימן' — Hebrew unit in English mode AND singular for a count of 697
findings.permutation: scope step STEP 3, Hebrew-Terms=English, font 1.0
findings.detail: The Mishnah Berurah scope item subtitle reads '697 סימן • Core section focus' (a11y confirmed). Two issues: the unit 'סימן' is Hebrew while terms=English (should be '697 Simanim' / '697 sections'), and it is the SINGULAR סימן for a count of 697 (should be plural סימנים). Arabic numeral + singular Hebrew noun + English tail in one line.

findings.title: Fresh sign-in / register forms show pre-filled masked password dots; reveal toggle does not unmask
findings.permutation: auth gate (Sign In + Create Account), fresh install, font 1.0
findings.detail: On a freshly-cleared install, the Sign In 'Secret Key' field and the Create Account 'Create Password' field both render with 8 masked dots (••••••••) while the email/name fields correctly show grey placeholders. This reads as 'a password is already entered' on an empty form (leftover/placeholder state). Tapping the eye/visibility toggle flips the icon to the 'shown' state but the field content stays as dots (onb_06_key_s.png) — the reveal does not unmask the placeholder, so the affordance looks broken. The underlying EditText text is genuinely empty (a11y), so these dots are a misleading placeholder pattern.

findings.title: 'Welcome Back!' sign-in copy shown to brand-new first-run users
findings.permutation: auth gate after fresh install + intro, font 1.0
findings.detail: After the three intro slides, a freshly-installed (just-cleared, re-seeded) user lands on a screen titled 'Welcome Back!' with subtitle 'Ready for your next learning adventure?' — returning-user copy for someone who has never had an account. The first-run primary action should bias toward register, not 'Welcome Back / Sign In'. 'Keep me signed in' is also pre-checked by default.

findings.title: Wizard allows advancing with ZERO study days selected (no validation)
findings.permutation: study days step STEP 4, all toggles off, font 1.0
findings.detail: I toggled all seven days (Sunday–שבת) OFF; the 'Continue' button stayed enabled and advanced to STEP 5 with zero study days. A pace-based goal with 0 study days/week is degenerate (progress impossible, estimate undefined), yet the wizard neither blocks it nor warns. Notably the later 'Estimated finish' still computed a date, implying the estimate ignores the study-days selection entirely.

findings.title: Redundant duplicated offline-warning banners stacked on Create Account (offline)
findings.permutation: register screen, offline (wifi+data disabled), font 1.0
findings.detail: When offline, the Create Account screen stacks two near-identical warning banners: 'Local account only: no cloud backup and no device sync.' immediately above 'No cloud backup or device sync. Your data stays only on this device.' — plus a third 'Offline mode: account stays only on this device.' acknowledge row. Three lines saying the same thing crowd the form and push fields below the fold.

findings.title: Silent failure: cloud registration against unreachable backend bounces back to Sign In with no error/snackbar
findings.permutation: register screen, online, font 1.0
findings.detail: Tapping 'Sign Up' online (Firebase-backed) showed a spinner for ~15s then returned to the 'Welcome Back!' Sign In screen with no visible success or error message. Per signup_screen.dart the success path sends a verification email and routes to Sign In, but from the UI the user gets zero feedback distinguishing success-needs-verification from failure — looks like a silent dead-end.

findings.title: Onboarding wizard primary buttons report empty accessibility bounds ([0,0][0,0])
findings.permutation: profile-creation + goal steps, font 1.0
findings.detail: uiautomator dumps show several primary CTAs ('Create Profile', 'Continue' on the goal step) with content-desc present but bounds='[0,0][0,0]', i.e. no laid-out hit rectangle in the accessibility tree. This breaks TalkBack focus/activation and made automated/precise tapping unreliable. Combined with the Continue/deadline tap collision above, it points at a layout/Semantics issue for these buttons.

findings.title: Carousel page-indicator dots are completely missing (IntroPageIndicator built + exported but never instantiated)
findings.permutation: all pages, font 1.0 and 1.3, both toggle states
findings.detail: No page-position dot row is rendered on ANY of the three intro pages — visually confirmed across all 9 captures. The user has no affordance telling them how many pages exist or which one they are on (only per-page progress bars labelled SETUP PROGRESS, which read as loading bars, not pagination). Code confirms why: lib/.../widgets/intro_page_indicator.dart defines IntroPageIndicator (documented as 'the canonical page position affordance'); app_intro_screen.dart re-exports it (lines 24-25) but NEVER constructs it in build(). grep shows the constructor 'IntroPageIndicator(' appears only in its own definition file. The widget is dead code; the prompt's listed 'page dots' control does not exist in the running UI.

findings.title: At font 1.3, rewards-page subtitle is occluded by the overlaid Get Started button on first view
findings.permutation: page 3 rewards / font 1.3 / hebrew-terms ON
findings.detail: On landing on page 3 at font_scale 1.3, the last line of the subtitle ('from a Novice to a תלמיד חכם!') renders UNDERNEATH the bottom 'Get Started' CTA, and the two feature cards (Badge/Mystery) are entirely hidden behind it. The CTA is a Positioned overlay (bottom:20) drawn on top of the scroll content, so the content is not clipped — scrolling reveals all of it — but a large-text user sees a half-hidden sentence behind the button on initial view. No RenderFlex overflow is logged (content is scrollable), so this is a layout/occlusion polish issue, not a hard clip.

findings.title: Device Back button on intro exits the app instead of stepping to the previous carousel page
findings.permutation: page 3 rewards / font 1.0 / hebrew-terms OFF (probe)
findings.detail: Pressing KEYCODE_BACK while on page 3 of the carousel backgrounded the app to the launcher (mCurrentFocus=nexuslauncher) rather than navigating page 3→2→1. The PageView has no Back interception. Re-launching restarts the carousel at page 1 (page position not preserved). No data loss (intro is stateless until Get Started), so low severity, but the Back behavior diverges from the common onboarding-carousel convention of stepping back through pages.

findings.title: No debounce on the Continue/Get Started CTA — rapid taps tunnel straight through onboarding and the permission prompt into Sign In
findings.permutation: page 1→Sign In / font 1.0 / hebrew-terms OFF (probe)
findings.detail: Five rapid back-to-back taps at the CTA coordinate advanced page1→2→3→Get Started, then a tap landed on the subsequently-pushed PermissionPrompt screen and dismissed it, finally landing on the Sign In screen — all from taps at one fixed point. No crash and no duplicate-route stack (single MainActivity, clean Sign In), so robustness is acceptable, but the lack of any tap debounce means a fast double-tap on 'Get Started' can blow past the onboarding permission prompt without the user seeing it.

findings.title: Default-ON Hebrew terms place a lone Hebrew-script word inside otherwise-English first-run copy (NOVICE / תלמיד חכם on one element)
findings.permutation: page 2 + page 3 / hebrew-terms ON (factory default)
findings.detail: HebrewTermsPreference.defaultValue == true, so a fresh first-run user sees mixed-script intro copy before being introduced to the app or given any chance to toggle: page-2 title 'Never Forget a משנה' and page-3 'climb from a Novice to a תלמיד חכם!', plus the Scholar Progress card showing English 'NOVICE' on the left endpoint and Hebrew 'תלמיד חכם' on the right endpoint of the SAME bar. This is design-intended (toggle default), and the oracle term-flip works correctly (see below), so it is reported as a polish/UX concern, not a rendering defect: there is no in-intro control to switch to all-Latin, and the lone Hebrew word in English chrome may read as a glitch to a first-time English user. Note the decorative chips 'Review…' and '…yos' on page 2 are intentional (hard-coded literals with baked-in ellipsis), NOT clipping bugs.

findings.title: First-run splash ('SYNCING YOUR PROGRESS') lingers ~20-30s on a no-network emulator before the intro appears
findings.permutation: pre-intro splash / both font scales
