findings.detail: Before AppIntro renders, a splash titled 'Master Your Learning, One Day at a Time / TORAH JOURNEY' with a 'PREPARING YOUR PATH… / SYNCING YOUR PROGRESS' progress bar sits with an unchanging frame (byte-identical screenshots) for ~20-30s on this offline emulator before transitioning. It does eventually advance (not a true hang). This is the splash screen, adjacent to but not part of AppIntro, so noted as context; on a real slow/no-network first launch the 'syncing' splash delay is user-visible and could be perceived as stuck.

findings.title: Onboarding permission-rationale screen is unreachable: authGuard rejects the route during first-run (no prompt ever shown to new users)
findings.permutation: fresh-install / no-account, first-run intro Skip path
findings.detail: app_intro_screen.dart:113 and onboarding_screen.dart:442 both push PermissionPromptRoute during onboarding, but app_router.dart:108-110 registers that route with guards:[authGuard]. auth_guard.dart only calls resolver.next() (allow) when kOnboardingComplete==true (line 44-48); otherwise (intro seen, no accounts) it does router.replace(SignInRoute) + resolver.next(false) (lines 67-73), REJECTING the permission-prompt navigation. During first-run, kOnboardingComplete is false at every onboarding push site, so the guard always diverts to SignIn. Empirically confirmed: tapping intro 'Skip' jumps straight to the 'Welcome Back' SignIn screen with the rationale screen never rendering. Net effect: the screen's own doc-comment promise ('shown once after profile creation') is defeated — brand-new users are NEVER shown the notifications/location rationale, and because app_intro sets kPermissionsPrompted=true (app_intro_screen.dart:114) right after the failed push, the later onboarding_screen push (gated on !alreadyPrompted, line 441) is also suppressed. POST_NOTIFICATIONS and ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION remain granted=false (confirmed via dumpsys), so users silently get no reminders and no local Shabbos times. A text-only loop that trusts the call sites would miss that the guard nullifies them.

findings.title: Permission rationale screen rendered only from Settings (post-onboarding) — the single guarded route has no onboarding-time entry that survives the guard
findings.permutation: source/architecture (all paths)
findings.detail: There is exactly ONE PermissionPromptRoute registration and it is auth-guarded. The only push site that runs after kOnboardingComplete becomes true is Settings -> App Permissions (settings_screen.dart:114). So the screen is de-facto a Settings-only surface despite being authored as an onboarding step. This is the root cause of the P1 above and means QA/visual coverage of the onboarding variant ('Almost Done!' title, 'Start Learning' CTA — permissionPromptTitleOnboarding / startLearning) can essentially never be seen by a real first-run user.

findings.title: Mixed-script body copy when Hebrew-terms toggle is ON (lone Hebrew word in an otherwise-English sentence) — chrome stays English due to known locale bug
findings.permutation: hebrew-terms toggle ON (source-verified; not pixel-verified)
findings.detail: With Hebrew-Terms ON, {shabbos}/{havdalah} resolve to Hebrew-script glyphs (שבת / הבדלה) embedded inside English sentences whose surrounding chrome (AppBar 'Almost Done!', card titles 'Notifications'/'Location', 'Allow', 'Start Learning') stay English because of the logged MaterialApp locale:null bug. The location card subtitle (permissionPromptLocationSubtitle, arb:2431) packs BOTH {shabbos} AND {havdalah} into one line, so two Hebrew terms sit inside one English sentence. By the oracle this is the intended toggle behavior (not a transliteration error), but the resulting half-translated card is a real UX smell worth design review. Could not pixel-confirm contrast/RTL handling of the embedded RTL Hebrew run inside an LTR English line — that requires rendering the screen, which was blocked.

findings.title: Font-scale 1.3 overflow risk on the dual-term location card is unverified (screen could not be rendered)
findings.permutation: font_scale 1.3 (not exercisable)
findings.detail: The location card subtitle 'Accurate {shabbos} candle-lighting and {havdalah} times based on your city.' is the longest string on the screen and at font_scale 1.3 (plus the Allow button and 44px icon consuming horizontal space) is the most likely place for vertical growth / a RenderFlex squeeze. The subtitle Text (line 263) sets no maxLines/ellipsis, so it should wrap rather than clip, but the card has fixed EdgeInsets.all(14) and the Row children could collide. This is flagged as a risk only — it could not be visually confirmed because the screen never rendered on this device.

findings.title: Standalone EmptyLoginScreen is unreachable — every zero-profile sign-in auto-creates a default learner profile and lands on the AppShell dashboard instead
findings.permutation: zero-profile account, online AND offline sign-in, with and without onboarding_skipped flag
findings.detail: EmptyLoginScreen (lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/empty_login_screen.dart) is documented as the surface 'shown when a user has zero profiles and previously skipped'. I constructed exactly that state by DB-editing the user account DB to zero learner_profiles and setting flutter.onboarding_skipped=true / onboarding_complete in prefs, then signed in via the AccountPicker. On EVERY attempt the app silently INSERTED a new learner_profiles row named after the account ('TestScholar', observed ids 2, 3, 4, 5 across 4 attempts) and routed to the AppShell dashboard — NEVER to the standalone EmptyLoginScreen. This happened identically offline (airplane mode on, confirmed by the airplane icon in /tmp/audit/relaunch.png) so it is NOT a Firestore cloud-pull repopulating the profile; it is a local default-profile bootstrap during sign-in/landing resolution. The sign-in resolver's EmptyLogin branch (sign_in_controller.dart lines 582 & 753-761, which require finalProfileCount==0) is therefore pre-empted and never fires. Net effect: the EmptyLogin surface — and its only unique controls (the 'I'm a tutor'/empty_login_tutor_entry OutlinedButton at lines 88-105, and the account-switch icon) — appear to be effectively dead/unreachable through normal app navigation. The only code path that renders it is the live onboarding 'Skip for now' tap (onboarding_screen.dart line 283, replaceAll([EmptyLoginRoute])), which I could not reach because sign-in auto-creates a profile before the onboarding wizard is ever shown.

findings.title: Zero-profile account shows full profile-scoped AppShell chrome (bottom nav + 'ADULT MODE' header) wrapping a 'you have no track/profile' empty state — context mismatch
findings.permutation: zero-profile account after sign-in (online & offline)
findings.detail: Because sign-in auto-creates a profile and lands on AppShell, the SkippedOnboardingCtaBanner ('Get started' / 'Add a learning track to begin tracking your progress.' / blue 'Add a learning track' CTA / 'Dismiss') renders INSIDE the dashboard scaffold — complete with the 'TestScholar / ADULT MODE' profile header (top), the account-switch chevron, and the DASHBOARD/LEARN/PROGRESS/SETTINGS bottom nav. The EmptyLoginScreen by contrast is a minimal Scaffold with an AppBar titled 'Learning Tracker', a Divider, and the tutor CTA, and intentionally has NO bottom nav. So a brand-new zero-profile user is shown the full profiled app shell (with PROGRESS/LEARN tabs that have no data and an 'ADULT MODE' badge for a profile that was silently auto-created) instead of the intended minimal onboarding-recovery surface. The banner content itself is visually clean (no clipping, overflow, low-contrast, or pluralization issues; waving-hand icon renders correctly), but it is being presented in the wrong navigational context for the empty/zero-profile case.

findings.title: Onboarding intro slide 2 mixes Hebrew-script term into English copy and shows a truncated/orphaned transliteration suffix ('Review… …yos')
findings.permutation: fresh-install first-run intro carousel (English UI, ashkenazi nusach default)
findings.detail: On the way to attempt the EmptyLogin path I passed through the first-run intro. Slide 2's headline rendered as 'Never Forget a משנה' — Hebrew-script characters (U+05DE U+05E9 U+05E0 U+05D4 = משנה) embedded in otherwise-English chrome while the Hebrew-terms toggle was OFF (default). Per the domain rubric, English-mode (transliteration) labels must not contain Hebrew-script unless intended, and the term should read 'Mishnah'/'Mishnayos'. The same card also exposed two fragmented strings 'Review…' and '…yos' (the ascender/descender of an ellipsized 'Mishnayos' broken across nodes), i.e. a transliteration suffix orphaned from its stem — consistent with text clipping/ellipsization. This is on the onboarding intro (adjacent to the empty-login flow), not the EmptyLogin screen itself, but it is a domain-oracle violation worth flagging given it gates the same first-run path.

findings.title: EmptyLogin 'Add a learning track' CTA would behave inconsistently with the screen's documented zero-profile precondition
findings.permutation: EmptyLogin reached with a non-empty profile list (e.g. via onboarding skip after a profile already exists)
findings.detail: Code-level corroboration of the reachability problem: EmptyLoginScreen's docstring states it is for accounts with ZERO profiles, yet its primary CTA (SkippedOnboardingCtaBanner) branches on profiles.isEmpty at runtime — if a profile exists it pushes TrackManagementHub, and only if empty does it show the 'Create a learner profile first' snackbar (ctaCreateProfileFirst) and route to ManageLearners. Given that the live path which actually renders EmptyLoginScreen is the onboarding 'Skip for now' tap (which can occur AFTER a profile row has been created earlier in the wizard), and given that sign-in auto-creates profiles, the screen can be reached in a state that contradicts its own zero-profile assumption, making the CTA's two branches reachable in the 'wrong' surface. I could not exercise the live tap (text-entry into Flutter fields via adb is not reliably injectable, blocking account creation to reach the onboarding intent chooser), so this is reported as a logic/inconsistency finding rather than a confirmed visual repro.

findings.title: BLOCKER: DeviceRestore screen is unreachable with the provided account — cloud sign-in routes to Onboarding instead, because every Firestore read returns PERMISSION_DENIED
findings.permutation: fresh-cleared device → sign in test-loop-a@orvex.test / TestLoop!2026 (reproduced twice + relaunch path)
findings.detail: On a freshly pm-cleared device, signing into the cloud account authenticates Firebase OK (top bar shows 'Loop Test A / ADULT MODE') but every Firestore pull fails. logcat: FirestorePermissionDeniedException (collection: completions, op: read) and 'Listen for QueryWrapper(users/WrUGgVgkhfRS5wdQJI5b0fb3Zjt2/learner_profiles) failed: PERMISSION_DENIED Missing or insufficient permissions', plus 'FirebaseContextProvider: Error getting App Check token. Error: Too many attempts.' SignInController._navigateAfterSignIn logs navigate_after_sign_in_pull_failed AND navigate_after_sign_in_fetch_profiles_failed, so cloudAccountHasProfiles=false, finalProfileCount=0 → router.replaceAll([OnboardingRoute]) (sign_in_controller.dart:614). The DeviceRestoreRoute is only reached when RestoreGuard intercepts a guarded shell-route navigation with 0 profiles + cloud account; the sign-in path diverts to Onboarding BEFORE that can happen, and on relaunch the AccountPicker→shell path logged restore_guard_new_device_check {completionCount:0, userProfileCount:1, isNewDevice:false} (a profile got created by the prior onboarding attempt). Net: with this account + this Firestore/App-Check state, the restore progress/retry/skip/error UI never renders. Needs either working Firestore permissions (so the cloud account has readable data and the new-device path engages) or a debug hook to force DeviceRestoreRoute. The iter3 'permanent blank' regression therefore could NOT be visually re-verified on-device this run; it is only confirmable by code review (see next finding).

findings.title: iter3 blank-screen risk: the 'idle' restore state renders SizedBox.shrink() — the screen is a literal blank when status is idle and the escape-hatch race loses
findings.permutation: code path: status==RestoreStatusIdle in build()
findings.detail: build()'s status.when idle branch returns SizedBox.shrink(), i.e. a fully blank Scaffold. The guard against a permanent blank is _startRestore(): if service.restore() returns false AND service.currentStatus is RestoreStatusIdle, it calls _navigateToApp(). This is the iter3 fix. But it is fragile: (a) it reads service.currentStatus synchronously after the awaited restore() — if the service emitted a non-idle-then-idle sequence, or restore() returns false for a non-idle reason not covered, the screen stays blank; (b) if deviceRestoreServiceProvider returns null (no cloud account / null gateway), _startRestore returns early at line 31 with NO navigation, leaving the screen on idle→SizedBox.shrink() forever. Reaching DeviceRestoreRoute with a null service (e.g. gateway briefly null during a rebuild) yields a permanent blank screen with no spinner, no text, no way out. Recommend the idle branch render a visible fallback (spinner + 'Preparing…') instead of SizedBox.shrink() so a blank can never be shown even if every escape path misses.

findings.title: Restore progress shows 'Step 0 of 3' on the first frame — a zero-indexed step count is nonsensical UX for a human-facing progress label
findings.permutation: restoring state, first phase 'Restoring your data...'
findings.detail: The service emits completedSteps 0,1,2 against totalSteps 3. The screen renders Text(l10n.deviceRestoreStep(completedSteps,totalSteps)) so the very first progress frame reads literally 'Step 0 of 3' (he: 'שלב 0 מתוך 3'), and the sequence is 0/3 → 1/3 → 2/3, never reaching '3 of 3' (it cuts to the green check). 'Step 0 of 3' reads as not-yet-started and the missing final step looks like a skipped step. Steps should be 1-indexed (Step 1/2/3 of 3) so the human sees a sane 1→3 progression. Could not screenshot live due to the P0 blocker, but it is deterministic from the emitted constants.

findings.title: Onboarding carousel (pre-restore flow) shows the same masechta in mixed nuschaos / ellipsized term badges
findings.permutation: fresh device onboarding intro, page 2 'Never Forget a משנה'
findings.detail: On the carousel page reached en-route to sign-in, the decorative term badges show '...yos' (top-right, Ashkenazi -os/-yos transliteration, ellipsized so the word is unreadable) alongside Hebrew-script 'משנה' in the headline 'Never Forget a משנה' and an English 'Review…' badge. This is an English-mode (UI locale English) surface mixing Hebrew script into the headline and ellipsizing a transliterated term to '...yos' which renders as nonsense. While this is the onboarding screen (not DeviceRestore itself), it sits directly on the path the restore-flow user traverses and violates the oracle rule that English-mode labels should not carry raw Hebrew script and that transliteration must not be clipped to an unreadable fragment. Worth flagging since the restore-flow audit traverses it.

findings.title: Long first-launch splash with no progress feedback — fresh device sits on 'PREPARING YOUR PATH' for ~47s extracting a 432 MB seed DB
findings.permutation: freshly pm-cleared device, first launch before any restore
findings.detail: After pm clear, the app holds on the 'PREPARING YOUR PATH… / SYNCING YOUR PROGRESS' splash for ~47 seconds while SeedManager extracts a 432.4 MB seed database. The splash's gradient bar is static and gives no indication of a long-running extraction, so on a real fresh device (the exact scenario that precedes DeviceRestore) the user faces a ~47s apparently-frozen screen with no progress %, no 'this can take a minute' copy. This is the pre-condition state for the restore flow and a likely abandonment/force-quit point. The restore flow's own progress UI is good by contrast; this seed-extract phase should show comparable progress feedback.

findings.title: Profile cards are grotesquely tall on tablet/landscape — ~60% of each card is empty whitespace (fixed childAspectRatio 0.67 mis-sized for wide columns)
findings.permutation: many-profiles x font1.0 AND font1.3 x tablet-landscape (2560x1600)
findings.detail: ProfileGrid (learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/profile_grid.dart:34-38) uses SliverGridDelegateWithFixedCrossAxisCount(crossAxisCount: 2, childAspectRatio: 0.67). On a wide tablet/landscape each of the 2 columns is ~1180px, so card height is forced to width/0.67 (~1760px) while the actual content (badge + 92px avatar + name + 'Tap to continue') is only ~300px tall. Result: every profile card AND the Add Profile card render as huge boxes with the content clustered at the top and ~60% empty whitespace below — only one grid row fits on screen at a time, forcing excessive scrolling. Reproducible at font 1.0 (not transient). The aspect ratio is tuned for narrow phone columns; the layout needs a width-aware aspect ratio (or a max card height / maxCrossAxisExtent delegate) for tablet.

findings.title: Profile display name is truncated with an ellipsis on phone-width cards at large font (full name only in a11y tree)
findings.permutation: many-profiles(3) x font1.3 x phone-portrait(1080x2400)
findings.detail:
ProfileCard (profile_card.dart:146-156) renders displayName with maxLines:1 + TextOverflow.ellipsis at fontSize 22. A profile named 'Menachem-Mendel-Yehoshua' renders visually as 'Menache…' on a phone-width 2-column card at font 1.3 — the learner cannot read or distinguish their own profile name. The uiautomator content-desc still carries the full name ('ADULT MODE
M
Menachem-Mendel-Yehoshua
...'), so the truncation is purely visual. Matches the batch-2 'name ellipsis here' note. Inconsistent with the profile switcher sheet, which wraps the same name to two lines (see /tmp/audit/pp_childswitch.png) rather than truncating.

findings.title: Child can escape CHILD MODE into an Adult profile and edit/delete any profile from the switcher with NO Parent PIN gate
findings.permutation: child profile selected (Shloime/CHILD MODE) -> header switcher (phone-portrait)
findings.detail: After selecting the child profile Shloime (CHILD MODE), tapping the dashboard header chip opens the profile switcher sheet (profile_switcher_sheet.dart) with NO Parent PIN challenge — even though a Parent PIN (1111) was set up during the child profile's creation. The sheet lists all profiles with per-row edit (pencil) and delete (trash) controls, a 'Switch account' row that exposes the account email, and 'Add Profile' / 'Skip to Settings'. Tapping the adult profile 'Avraham' switched straight into ADULT MODE with no PIN prompt (/tmp/audit/pp_child2adult.png). This defeats the purpose of child mode + parent PIN: a child can leave child mode, open adult surfaces, switch account, or delete profiles unsupervised. (Surfaces from the profile-selection system adjacent to the picker; the same switcher is reachable from the picker's header chip.)

findings.title: Picker header asserts a stale/wrong active identity ('AuditParent · ADULT MODE') while the screen's whole purpose is that no profile is selected yet
findings.permutation: many-profiles x picker entry (no profile selected) x both widths/fonts
findings.detail: The ProfilePicker is reached precisely because ProfileGuard found 2+ profiles and NO selected profile, yet the persistent top app bar over the picker shows 'A  AuditParent' with an 'ADULT MODE' badge and a profile-switcher chevron. 'AuditParent' is the ACCOUNT display name (entered at signup) — it is NOT the name of any of the 3 learner profiles (Avraham/Shloime/Menachem...). So the header (a) shows an account name where a profile is implied and (b) shows a profile-MODE badge ('ADULT MODE') before any profile/mode has been chosen, defaulting to the profile-0 sentinel. After a profile is actually picked the header corrects (e.g. 'Shloime · CHILD MODE', /tmp/audit/pp_childsel.png), confirming the picker-state header is stale/defaulted context.

findings.title: System Back on the picker exits the app to the launcher (no in-picker back affordance)
findings.permutation: many-profiles x picker x Back button
findings.detail: Pressing the Android system Back button on the ProfilePicker drops the user out of the app to the home launcher (mCurrentFocus became com.google.android.apps.nexuslauncher after the keyevent). The picker is a replaceAll root route with no AppBar back button, so the only forward nav is selecting a profile, Add Profile, the (stale) header switcher chip, or Skip to Settings. Exiting to launcher on Back is defensible for a root gate, but combined with the misleading header it means a user who lands here with no obvious 'back/cancel' can only escape the app entirely. Worth a deliberate decision (no-op, or route to a sensible parent) rather than implicit app-exit.

findings.title: Add Profile card label wraps to two lines ('Add'/'Profile') — cosmetic, no clipping
findings.permutation: many-profiles x font1.0/1.3 x tablet AND phone
findings.detail: The Add Profile card title 'Add Profile' (add_profile_card.dart) wraps onto two lines on the narrow card cell. It is NOT clipped or ellipsized (the card uses FittedBox(scaleDown) + headlineSmall), so this is purely a cosmetic wrap rather than a defect, but it reads slightly awkwardly ('Add' over 'Profile') and is inconsistent with the single-line title intent. Low priority; noting for completeness.

findings.title: City subtitle shows raw GeoNames admin1 CODE (e.g. "06", "11", "08") instead of a region name for every non-US country; the nonsense value persists into the saved Sacred Time location
findings.permutation: data: single + multi-result, font 1.0 and 1.3
findings.detail: Each result row subtitle is built by _subtitleFor() as `admin1 · countryCode`. The bundled cities.sqlite stores GeoNames field index 10 = the admin1 CODE (verified in tool/build_cities_db.dart:81 `final admin1 = f[10]`), NOT the human-readable admin1 name (which lives in the separate admin1CodesASCII.txt lookup that was never joined). For the US, GeoNames admin1 codes coincide with 2-letter state postal abbreviations so they read fine ("New York City / NY · US", "San Diego / CA · US"). For every other country the code is an opaque number: Jerusalem → "06 · IL", Paris (all 8 arrondissement rows) → "11 · FR", London (Canada) → "08 · CA", Santo Domingo → "34 · DO", Sanaa → "26 · YE", Santa Cruz de la Sierra → "08 · BO", Santiago de Querétaro → "22 · MX", New Territories → "00 · HK". On the "London" search the inconsistency is glaring on ONE screen: "London / ENG · GB" (UK, readable) sits directly above "London / 08 · CA" (Canada, raw code) — the subtitle is supposed to disambiguate identical city names but for the Canadian one it is meaningless. For Paris, all 8 rows share "11 · FR", giving the subtitle zero disambiguation value. Worse, the raw code is NOT transient: selecting Jerusalem persists the label and Settings then shows "Jerusalem, 06, IL  /  Chosen from city list" (and selecting Santiago shows "Santiago, 12, CL"). So a religious user setting their location for Shabbos/Yom-Tov candle-lighting times sees a permanent meaningless "06" in their saved city. The raw code also leaks into the accessibility label (content-desc="Jerusalem\n06 · IL"), so screen-reader users hear "Jerusalem, zero six, IL". Fix: join admin1 code → name via admin1CodesASCII at DB-build time, or fall back to bare countryCode when no readable region name is available.

findings.title: Search field has no clear/X affordance — the only way to clear a typed query is manual backspacing
findings.permutation: data: any populated query, font 1.0/1.3
findings.detail: The picker's TextField (city_picker_screen.dart:47-62) defines only a prefixIcon (search) — no suffixIcon clear button and no clear handler. Once a query is typed (e.g. "New York", or a 57-char junk string), there is no one-tap way to reset to the idle "~33,000 cities" hint; the user must hold backspace. The audit brief explicitly lists "clear" as a control to exercise, and it simply does not exist on this screen. Minor usability gap; common pattern for typeahead search fields is a trailing X when text is non-empty.

findings.title: Stale 'STEP 1 OF N' denominator after selecting a program-bearing curriculum then backing up
findings.permutation: Hebrew-terms OFF, font 1.3, Sephardi (reproduced across font scales)
findings.detail: On first entry the curriculum-select header reads 'STEP 1 OF 6'. Selecting a curriculum that owns a study program (Mussar -> Chofetz Chaim Daily; also Bavli/Nach) expands the flow to 7 steps and advances to 'STEP 2 OF 7 — Join a Program?'. Pressing Back returns to Step 1 but the header now reads 'STEP 1 OF 7' even though NO curriculum is currently selected and 0% progress is shown. The inflated total (7) is wrong for the neutral Step-1 state — it should revert to 'OF 6' until a program-bearing curriculum is actually chosen. Confirmed not transient: a clean re-entry into the flow correctly shows 'OF 6'. User-visible inconsistency: a user who picks Mussar/Bavli/Nach, reconsiders, and goes back sees a step count that no longer matches their (empty) selection.

findings.title: Curriculum-select layout is fully clean across all nusach/terms/font permutations (positive verification)
findings.permutation: all five permutations
findings.detail: Reported as a finding only to document the exhaustive negative result the rubric asks for. No clipping, no mid-word breaks, no RenderFlex overflow stripes (logcat confirms zero overflow exceptions), no low-contrast text, no blank icon discs (all 9 glyphs render: book/gavel/document/account_balance/self_improvement/auto_stories), no overlapping/colliding tap targets. The longest English name 'Talmud Yerushalmi' wraps to two lines and the row card grows to fit at font 1.3; the longest Hebrew name 'תלמוד ירושלמי' stays on one line. Hebrew rows are right-aligned (RTL) while the icon stays left and chevron stays right — consistent with the already-logged MaterialApp locale:null chrome-stays-LTR limitation, not a new defect.

findings.title: Collision 'Cancel — keep offline account' button does NOT keep the offline account or leave the flow (label/behavior mismatch)
findings.permutation: _PhaseCollision (code-reviewed; not reachable offline)
findings.detail: In _CollisionBlock the TextButton is labelled with l10n key upgradeToCloudCancelKeepOffline ('Cancel — keep offline account'), but its onCancel resets _phase to `const _PhaseCollision()` — i.e. it stays INSIDE the collision warning block (just clears the chosen option and the cloud-password field). It does NOT return the user to the form or out of the upgrade flow, and it does not 'keep the offline account' in any observable way. The only escape is the AppBar back arrow. Compare _VerificationRequiredBlock whose onCancel correctly does `setState(() => _phase = const _PhaseForm())` (lines 395-396). The collision-phase cancel is both mislabeled and inconsistent with the verification-phase cancel, leaving the user effectively trapped on the scary red 'A cloud account already exists' warning with a CTA that appears to be the safe exit but isn't.

findings.title: Screen is almost entirely hardcoded English; only ~4 strings are localized
findings.permutation: all phases
findings.detail: Only upgradeToCloudTitle, upgradeToCloudButton, upgradeToCloudCancelKeepOffline and the verification toast (errorVerificationEmailSent) come from AppLocalizations. Everything else is hardcoded English literals: heading 'Back up your account', the entire 'You're signed in as … one-way …' body, field label 'Confirm your password', validator 'Password required', errors 'Incorrect password.'/'Upgrade failed: …'/the two internet-required messages, the whole collision block (titles, both option tiles, checkbox text, 'Upload and sign in'/'Discard local and sign in'), and the success block ('You're backed up!', 'Your data will now sync across devices automatically.'). he.arb DOES contain Hebrew for the few localized keys, so under a Hebrew locale this screen would render a jarring English/Hebrew mix. Latent today only because of the known MaterialApp locale:null bug, but it is real i18n debt and the L1 test comments explicitly flag each hardcoded string.

findings.title: Stale validation/error text persists after the field is corrected
findings.permutation: _PhaseForm, font 1.0
findings.detail: After an empty-submit shows 'Password required' (red field outline), typing a valid password does NOT clear the error — the red 'Password required' text and red outline remain until the next submit re-runs validate(). Likewise the offline 'Internet connection is required…' error sits below the field while the user edits/retypes. Standard Flutter autovalidate behavior, but visually it reads as 'still wrong' even though the input is now valid; an autovalidateMode of onUserInteraction (or clearing the error in onChanged) would fix it.

findings.title: Collision / Verification / Success phases unverifiable on this device (no network to Firebase)
findings.permutation: _PhaseCollision, _PhaseVerifying, _PhaseSuccess
findings.detail: The emulator has no real internet route (airplane mode OFF but network unreachable), so the connectivity guard short-circuits every submit before any Firebase call. The three post-network phases — email-collision resolution UI (radio tiles + cloud-password field + discard-acknowledge checkbox + execute buttons), the email-verification panel, and the success block — can never render here. These are also the screen's highest visual-overflow risk (densest layout) and the L1 widget tests skip them due to an argon2id Isolate limitation, so they are the least-verified surfaces. Recommend a follow-up pass on a device with Firebase connectivity (or a forced-state harness) to vision-audit those three blocks at font 1.0 and 1.3.
